الانتماءات (affiliations): Medizinische Hochschule Hannover; Tehran University of Medical Sciences; Technische Universität Braunschweig; Heidelberg University; Indian Institute of Technology Hyderabad
الكلمات المفتاحية (author_keywords): track and trigger systems; clinical deterioration detection; levels of automation; predictive algorithms; machine learning; vital signs monitoring; ICU transfer; mortality prediction; interoperability; electronic health records; wearable devices; rapid response teams
الملخص (abstract): Background: Electronic early warning/track-and-trigger systems (EW/TTS) are crucial for patient monitoring, detecting clinical deterioration (CD), and activating rapid response teams. Understanding the current level of automation in EW/TTS is essential. Objective: This study aimed to provide a comprehensive overview and critical assessment of electronic EW/TTS, including automated features, algorithms, and technologies, following a published registered study protocol. Methods: Based on the PRISMA (Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses) guidelines, we included studies from PubMed, Web of Science, and Scopus published between January 2010 and December 2025 describing EW/TTS applied in real-world settings, and electronic systems for CD detection. We excluded studies outside the clinical context or those that used manual scoring charts. We applied a descriptive narrative approach and a methodological quality assessment according to the Joanna Briggs Institute Critical Appraisal Checklist. Results: After removing outliers and duplicates, the query returned 1181 studies. The selected studies (n=43) reported CD as the primary objective in 24 of 44 (54.5%) reported primary objectives, with ICU transfer in 16 of 68 (23.5%) reported secondary objectives, and mortality prediction in 10 of 68 (14.7%) reported secondary objectives. EW/TTS primarily relied on vital signs and assessment scores, accounting for 42 of 67 (62.7%) reported clinical indexes to detect and predict CD effectively. Among the included systems, 18 of 43 (41.9%) had a measured automation level, 11 of 43 (25.6%) had a managed automation level, and 7 of 43 (16.3%) had a defined automation level. The studies focused on several technological domains, with a strong emphasis on data analytics (24/43, 55.8%) and hardware technologies (7/43, 16.3%). Predictive algorithms, including statistical and machine learning approaches, were used in 11 of 43 (25.6%) systems. Interoperable connectivity was reported in 30 of 43 (69.8%) systems, including connectivity with electronic health records, wearable devices, and communication platforms such as Ascom Unite, as well as integrations using standards such as Health Level Seven Fast Healthcare Interoperability Resource and Health Level Seven. Evaluations of the systems showed earlier warning (14/70, 20%), higher accuracy (12/70, 17.1%), and lower specificity (9/70, 12.9%) as the main reported outcomes. Electronic EW/TTS were most prevalent in the United States (15/43, 34.9%), the United Kingdom (6/43, 14%), and the Netherlands (6/43, 14%). Conclusions: Current EW/TTS systems implemented a measured level of automation and primarily focused on patient monitoring in hospital surgery wards. More than half of EW/TTS featured data exchange capabilities and connectivity with other systems. Reported outcomes of EW/TTS included early warning, high accuracy, and lower specificity. However, the included evidence was limited by heterogeneous prediction targets, inconsistent performance metrics and time horizons, and poor reporting of development history and system failure. Using clinically validated wearable devices and establishing a standardized data collection framework may further improve system accuracy and reliability.

الملخص (abstract): Crude oil wastewater contains complex contaminants that pose significant environmental and health risks. Conventional ultrafiltration membranes exhibit limited hydrophilicity, susceptibility to fouling, and low permeability, thereby limiting their filtration efficiency. This study aims to develop a high-performance ultrafiltration membrane with enhanced hydrophilicity, permeability, and antifouling properties for effective oil–water separation. A polyvinylidene fluoride–polypyrrole–nanoclay (PVDF–PPy–NC) composite membrane was fabricated via a simple two-step approach. Membranes with varying nanoclay loadings (0.05–0.15 wt%) were prepared and evaluated under ultrafiltration conditions (1 bar, 23 ± 2°C) and pH=8.2. Incorporating PPy and nanoclay significantly improved membrane performance, with enhanced hydrophilicity (contact angle reduced from 88° to 71.6°), increased porosity (from 59.5% to 85.86%), and higher water flux (up to 324.5 LMH). The membrane containing 0.1 wt% nanoclay (Pyc-0.1) exhibited optimal performance, owing to uniform nanoclay dispersion that promoted a favorable pore structure. Conversely, excessive loading (0.15 wt%) led to nanoclay aggregation, resulting in irregular pores and a decline in flux. All modified membranes achieved high oil rejection (> 99.5%) and improved antifouling performance. These results demonstrate the potential of the fabricated membranes as cost-effective, scalable candidates for industrial oily wastewater treatment, particularly in petroleum production, thereby contributing to more sustainable water management practices.

الملخص (abstract): This investigation aimed to explore novel theoretical aspects and applications of the information-generating function measure for order statistics. We developed fundamental properties and established stochastic ordering relationships based on this information-theoretic measure. Our analysis demonstrated that when two order statistics share identical information-generating measures, their underlying parent distributions can be uniquely identified. We implemented our proposed measure to characterize the exponential distribution. Moreover, we derived bounds and investigated monotonicity properties for these functional measures. The study further examined how information-generating functions characterize distributional symmetry, with particular applications to uniform and normal distributions for identifying symmetry points of order statistics. Building on these theoretical foundations, we proposed a new symmetry test statistic derived from the information-generating properties of the order statistics. Using comprehensive Monte Carlo simulations, we evaluated the test's statistical power against existing alternatives. The present results demonstrated superior performance across various asymmetric distributional alternatives. The practical utility of our methodology is illustrated through an empirical analysis of chronic disease prevalence data.

الملخص (abstract): In this article, we investigate the domination properties of the commuting graph Gamma(M(m circle plus m, L)). Specifically, we determine the domination number gamma(Gamma(M(m circle plus m, L))) and establish sharp bounds for various classes of finite commutative rings with unity. Our main result demonstrates that for any such ring L, the domination number satisfies the inequality gamma(Gamma(M(m circle plus m, L))) >= 2. These results contribute to the broader study of graph-theoretic properties of algebraic structures and have applications in coding theory and algebraic combinatorics.

العنوان (title): Mistaken instant transfers in Jordan: From unjust enrichment to criminal liability
المؤلفون (authors): Hamzeh M. Abu Issa; Fatiha Mohammed Gourari; Tariq kamal Alhasan; Maen Abdel-Rahim Juwaihan; Mohammad Nasr Khater
الانتماءات (affiliations): Applied Science Private University; United Arab Emirates University; Petra University
الكلمات المفتاحية (author_keywords): instant payment systems; unjust enrichment; criminal liability; conversion; Jordan; restitution
الملخص (abstract): Wrong-recipient transfers in instant-payment systems involve correct execution of an authenticated order but a payer’s mistake as to the beneficiary identifier. Jordanian practice oscillates between treating the outcome as civil undue payment and escalating to criminal proceedings when the recipient retains the funds. This article develops a sequenced account that separates (1) execution under the payment-service contract, (2) private-law entitlement to the credit, and (3) conditions for penal attribution. It anchors that sequence in the doctrine of causa in obligations, unjust enrichment and payment of the undue, and it reads Penal Code Article 424 against Jordanian judgments and comparative wrongful-credit models. As a matter of private law, a misdirected transfer does not extinguish the payer’s debt to the intended creditor unless performance reached that creditor or an authorised representative; the mistaken beneficiary’s enrichment is prima facie without causa and triggers restitution. As a matter of criminal attribution, the initiating transfer is voluntary, so liability should not be built through expansive theft or fraud analogies. Article 424 should apply only after a provable knowledge/notice point at which the recipient actually learns of the mistake and then engages in conversion. The proposed Article 424 checklist is cumulative as to mistaken receipt, actual knowledge and post-knowledge conversion, while the listed conversion behaviours are alternative indicators of the same material element. The result is a workable boundary that preserves civil autonomy, targets opportunistic retention, clarifies the burden of proving notice, and supports regulatory guidance for banks and payment service providers.

الملخص (abstract): This paper presents an experimental investigation of continuous reinforced beams strengthened with carbon fibre reinforced polymer ropes. The test specimens included six full-scale reinforced concrete beams; one control specimen without strengthening, while the other five specimens were strengthened externally with CFRP ropes. The ratio of CFRP ropes to the internal steel reinforcement at both mid-span and middle support regions was the main parameter investigated. The main aim of this study was to evaluate how the mechanical characteristics of the CFRP reinforcement system influence structural performance by assessing the impact of CFRP ropes on stiffness, flexural strength, ductility, and moment redistribution. The results showed that adding CFRP ropes to continuous RC beams improved flexural stiffness, load-carrying capacity up to 27.8 %, and moment distribution by 18.9 % due to increased ductility. Experimental: results were compared with load and deflection predictions from both the ACI design guidelines and a theoretical model. While ACI 440.2R-17 provided reasonably accurate predictions of flexural capacity, ACI 440.1R-06 and ACI 440.1R-15 significantly underestimated deflections, especially after cracking occurred. However, the deflection estimation from the theoretical model was in good agreement with the experimental results.

كلمات الفهرسة (keywords_plus): INDUCED MEMORY IMPAIRMENT; BETA PEPTIDE; RIVASTIGMINE; INSULIN; ACETYLCHOLINESTERASE; INHIBITION; MODULATION; GSK3-BETA; DEMENTIA; SYNTHASE
الملخص (abstract): The strong relationship between Alzheimer's Disease (AD) and diabetes mellitus (DM) is described by the term "type 3 diabetes". Canagliflozin (CAN), a sodium-glucose co-transporter 2 inhibitor (SGLT2i), is an antidiabetic agent under investigation as a potential new treatment for AD due to its acetylcholinesterase (AChE) inhibitory properties. We aimed to examine the effect of CAN on the efficacy of the anti-acetylcholinesterase, rivastigmine (RIV), against aluminum chloride (AlCl3)-induced AD rat model. The efficacy of CAN, RIV, and CAN plus RIV against abnormal behavioral, biochemical, and histological changes in AlCl3-induced AD in rats was examined. Three weeks of treatment with CAN partially reversed the AlCl3-induced behavioral dysfunction, along with significantly elevated levels of brain-derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF) and decreased levels of AChE, glycogen synthase kinase-3 beta (GSK3 beta), amyloid beta (A beta) deposits, and inducible nitric oxide synthase (iNOS) expression. Histological examination revealed that CAN administration significantly increased RIV's efficacy by protecting neurons in rats' hippocampal tissues from AlCl3-induced damage. Interestingly, the RIV + CAN combination exhibited a more pronounced inhibitory effect on A beta plaque formation, iNOS activity, and neurodegeneration compared to either RIV or CAN alone. However, this combination did not show any additive benefits for behavior, AChE activity, BDNF, or GSK3 beta concentrations compared with RIV alone. Our research indicates that CAN has potential benefits for AD, as evidenced by improvements in cognitive abilities, cholinergic activity, and neurogenesis in rats with AD. This is attributed to the upregulation of BDNF/GSK3 beta signaling, reduced neuroinflammation, and A beta deposition.

الملخص (abstract): AI-driven smart urban environments increasingly deliver mobility and utility services through public Wi-Fi, QR touchpoints, kiosks, and IoT-enabled interfaces. These brief, time-pressured interactions create an ambient, citizen-facing attack surface where social engineering and deceptive touchpoints—QR substitution, rogue access points, account takeover, and spoofed civic messages—can cause harm without exploiting classic software flaws. This paper proposes C3H (Citizen-Centric Cyber Hygiene), a shared-responsibility framework that couples low-friction citizen micro-behaviors with municipal safeguards. C3H organizes defenses across three layers: Identity (minimal disclosure and phishing-resistant authentication), Edge/IoT Interaction (verifiable civic artifacts and safer public connectivity), and Algorithmic Awareness (authenticated communications plus contestability for AI-mediated services). We present a citizen-focused risk taxonomy and a mapping from hygiene behaviors to city-side controls, demonstrated through a smart bus-stop scenario. Finally, we examine adoption barriers in developing contexts (trust deficits, digital divides, legacy devices) using Jordan/Amman as a representative case and contrasting citizen-centric initiatives in Dubai.

Using a two-anchor longitudinal policy analysis, it contrasts a 2015 baseline documented in contemporaneous assessment materials—marked by siloed decision-making, project-by-project financing, and weak data interoperability—with a January 2026 snapshot drawn mainly from municipal and national strategy documents. The 2026 materials articulate governance mechanisms designed to enable scaling, including portfolio coordination, platform-oriented data integration via a proposed Urban Observatory, and proposed KPI-linked performance monitoring. الملخص (abstract): Urban transport modernization increasingly depends on tightly coupled cyber–physical services linking vehicles, stations, roadside monitoring, passenger applications, and back-office control. Integration can raise efficiency and strengthen safety oversight, yet it expands the attack surface and enables cascading failures that interrupt service and reduce public confidence. This paper proposes a conceptual framework for cyber-resilient integrated transport operations, using Amman’s BRT transition as a practical reference. It offers: (i) a transport-oriented threat-surface and trust-boundary model spanning field, edge, and core domains; (ii) a reference architecture for AI-enabled zero trust monitoring that binds telemetry to identity, performs edge screening and core correlation, and links detections to operationally safe containment actions; and (iii) a validation plan with measurable objectives and staged evaluation using public datasets, digital-twin scenarios, and privacy-preserving pilots. الملخص (abstract): Smart city frameworks frequently include a "Smart People" dimension (education, creativity, civic engagement), yet it is often treated as an aspirational attribute rather than a public capability built through durable institutions. This paper re-reads "Smart People" as an inclusion project by examining a policy trajectory in Jordan: the development of Knowledge Stations—community technology centers described in official communications as launched in 2001 to support rural and under-served communities—and their upgrading/reframing as "Future Stations" under a national strategy and executive plan (2025– 2028). Using a sociological lens on digital inclusion and education technology, we synthesize scholarship on multi-level digital divides, digital capital and digital human capital, and critical smart city governance to analyze how upskilling infrastructures redefine participation in the digital economy and the state. Empirically, we triangulate public program communications on (i) Future Stations’ emphasis on advanced digital skills, entrepreneurship, and digital government access, and (ii) Jordan’s public-sector AI capacity-building targets and reported training volumes. Because official reporting distinguishes partially overlapping categories (e.g., AI awareness vs. AI technologies training), we treat figures as parallel signals rather than additive totals. We argue that the shift from basic digital literacy to AI readiness can expand opportunity, but it also risks an AI-conversion divide in which inequality hinges on whether AI-related skills translate into valued labor-market outcomes and legitimate participation in AI-mediated governance. We conclude with design principles and evaluation metrics for inclusive AI-ready community hubs.

الملخص (abstract): Arid controlled-environment agriculture (CEA) in the Middle East and North Africa (MENA) couples electricity for cooling with water for irrigation and evaporative cooling, under tight budgets and unreliable connectivity. This paper presents MENA-Twin, a security-aware edge-AI and digital-twin framework that jointly optimizes this water–energy nexus. It models actors, assets, interactions, threats, governance constraints, and control options as a linked semantic system that shapes state construction, action boundaries, reward design, explainability, and cross-platform learning. الملخص (abstract): Critical infrastructure incident response increasingly relies on automation to contain cyber-physical threats under time pressure. Reinforcement learning (RL) is attractive for response selection because it can adapt to evolving attack sequences and can mitigate partial observability when the state is augmented with short telemetry and alert history (or when recurrent value networks are used), yet RL policies are typically opaque and therefore difficult to justify in safety-critical operations. This paper develops an explainable reinforcement learning (XRL) framework for automated incident response in supervisory control and data acquisition (SCADA) environments. The framework couples a Deep Q-Network (DQN) response agent with (i) an explicit safety shield that enforces operational constraints and (ii) a post-hoc Explainer Module that produces feature-attribution explanations using Shapley Additive Explanations (SHAP). We specify how SHAP attributions are extracted from the DQN decision process by mapping the selected action’s Q-value to a scalar explanation target, using background states drawn from a governed replay buffer or historian, and applying a latency-bounded gradient-based SHAP approximation (e.g., DeepSHAP/GradientSHAP implementations). We further propose a SCADA control-room workflow in which the agent remains advisory by default, supports graded autonomy for low-risk actions, and produces audit-ready explanation artifacts that align with operator mental models and regulatory expectations. We describe an experimental setup grounded in established industrial datasets (SWaT/WADI and hardware-in-the-loop water distribution data) and testbed practices, and we provide an evaluation plan and indicative findings emphasizing response timeliness, unsafe actuation avoidance, and operator override behavior. The contribution is a precise architecture and operator-centered workflow for deploying XRL in critical infrastructure without relying on undocumented assumptions about autonomy.

الملخص (abstract): Vehicular ad hoc networks need rapid authentication under short contacts, intermittent backhaul, and roaming across operators. Kerberos provides efficient ticket-based session keys, but it assumes reachable domain KDCs and offers limited cross-operator audit and revocation. RSUs validate Kerberos tickets locally and consult the ledger only when roaming or risk policy requires it. We specify the protocol workflow, RSU decision logic, and a minimal smart contract for registration, verification, and revocation. We also outline an evaluation plan and practical feasibility considerations.

Because data availability varies widely across cities, we also discuss data-readiness tiers and fallback strategies for contexts where BIM, IoT streams, or semantic 3D city models are incomplete, fragmented, or unavailable.

الملخص (abstract): The interaction between human beings and computers is changing in the fields of healthcare, education, and entertainment with the help of Extended Reality technologies. Nevertheless, there are serious issues of accessibility, safety and user sovereignty that pose a threat to equitable adoption. The chapter offers an inclusive Trustworthy XR Framework to such interrelated issues by means of empirical analysis of publicly accessible datasets such as BOXRR-23 motion capture data, cybersickness physiological records, and XR accessibility test protocols. الملخص (abstract): Metaverse ecosystems pose new challenges that have never been seen before in ensuring that digital identities are consistent across heterogeneous platforms. The chapter suggests a new twin architecture based on the digital twin principles of managing identity that introduces a federated model that includes credential, behavioral, context, and authorization sub-twins. In our methodology, we use privacy-preserving protocols of synchronization using zero-knowledge proofs. On benchmark datasets (LFW, VGGFace2, KeyRecs) the system has been shown to achieve 99.1% authentication accuracy, 0.7% EER (22% better than current systems) and 127ms average latency and 99.8% cross-platform synchronization reliability. These results provide a roadmap to the next-generation authentication systems that would enable the smooth experiences across the physical-virtual metaverse boundaries.

الملخص (abstract): Intelligent User Interfaces (IUIs) represent a paradigm shift in human-computer interaction, leveraging artificial intelligence to create adaptive, personalized, and context-aware systems. The proliferation of multimodal interaction paradigms, combined with advances in machine learning and large language models, has created unprecedented opportunities for enhancing user experience across diverse application domains. However, current implementations suffer from fragmented approaches, limited adaptability, and inadequate integration of emerging technologies. This paper proposes a comprehensive framework integrating multimodal input processing, reinforcement learning-based adaptation, context-aware personalization, and explainable AI components. We conduct extensive experiments using the Rico mobile UI dataset, human-machine interaction benchmarks, and custom multimodal datasets comprising 61,358 interaction sessions from 2,867 users. Our proposed framework achieves significant improvements over baseline approaches, demonstrating 93.4% task completion rate (22.2% improvement over static interfaces), 91.2% user satisfaction score, 88.1% adaptation accuracy, and 83.5% context awareness precision. The system reduces average response latency by 47% compared to traditional adaptive interfaces while maintaining explainability through integrated XAI modules. User studies with 120 participants confirm that explainability features increase trust by 87%. These findings establish a foundation for next-generation IUI systems capable of seamlessly adapting to user needs, preferences, and contextual factors while maintaining transparency and accountability.

الكلمات المفتاحية (author_keywords): social presence; digital twin; haptic feedback; metaverse; gesture tracking; spatial audio; user experience; learnability; navigability; task completion time; novice vs expert users
الملخص (abstract): The fusion of physical and virtual worlds opens up unexampled prospects for social contact by means of embodied presence. Present metaverse platforms allow for very lively participation, but the gap between feelings in the real world and their representation in the game leaves actual interpersonal communication unfulfilled. This paper suggests a completely new setup for cross-realm embodied interactions making use of synchronized haptic feedback together with digital twin technology to set up bidirectional presence across both the physical and virtual domains. A prototype system is composed of real-time gesture tracking, tactile actuation, and spatial audio rendering to support social exchanges, such as handshakes or other gestures and collective object manipulation. A controlled study on the investigation of user experience in motivation, satisfaction, usability, learnability, and navigability dimensions with 16 participants has been performed. Motivation (M=4.2, SD=0.6) and satisfaction (M=4.1, SD=0.5) ratings have proved to be rather high while usability rating is more of a moderate value (M=3.8, SD=0.7). But learnability (M=3.2, SD=0.8) and navigability (M=3.1, SD=0.9) scored lower because this new haptic gesture interface replaced the old way of inputting commands. There is a statistically significant difference between the two groups, novice and expert users, in terms of task completion time and error rate; p<0.01 for time and p<0.05 for error rate. Results show that perceived social presence improved by 34% when haptic feedback was included compared to a baseline of visual-only interaction. The current work empirically informs critical challenges toward designing for cross-realm social platforms that require haptic interfaces for embodied virtual communication.

العنوان (title): A Conceptual Model for Integrating AI and Metaverse in Education
المجلة أو المؤتمر (venue): International Conference on Computational Intelligence Approaches and Applications (ICCIAA)

الملخص (abstract): The fast development of artificial intelligence (AI) and metaverse technologies opens the previously unheard-of opportunities to change the paradigm of education. Nevertheless, the application of these technologies to educational ecosystems is still dispersed and does not have a holistic theoretical basis with empirical evidence. This gap is filled in this paper by suggesting a new four-layer conceptual model that integrates AI capabilities and metaverse environments in a systematic way to develop adaptive, immersive, and personalized learning experiences. Our model includes four layers that are interrelated, namely: the Infrastructure Layer, which represents the technological base; the Intelligence Layer, which includes AI-based personalization and analytics; the Immersion Layer, which applies metaverse-based technologies to experiential learning; and the Pedagogical Layer, which makes the model consistent with the educational goals. Our model was tested with the help of three large-scale educational datasets: HarvardX-MITx MOOC dataset (641,138 student enrollments), UCI Student Performance dataset (1, 044 students), and Open University Learning Analytics Dataset (OULAD, 32,593 students). Through machine learning classification, correlation analysis and structural equation modeling, we demonstrated that courses and learning environments that are more consistent with our four-layer model performed much better. The completion rates (210% higher), engagement duration (79 vs 4.7 weeks), and assessment success rates (34 vs 58.3% higher) were also increased in enhanced courses than in minimal-feature courses. Analysis of importance of features showed that Intelligence and Immersion layers have 64 percent predictive power on student success.

الملخص (abstract): In today's digital landscape, cybercriminals are increasingly leveraging artificial intelligence to outsmart traditional security systems, creating an urgent need for more sophisticated defense mechanisms. This paper introduces AMADEUS, an innovative cybersecurity framework that fights AI-powered threats with advanced machine learning techniques. AMADEUS operates like a coordinated team of digital security guards—some agents actively hunt for threats, others coordinate defensive responses, and all continuously learn from each attack to improve future protection. What sets AMADEUS apart is its ability to learn and adapt in real-time while maintaining lightning-fast threat detection capabilities. Through extensive testing on three major cybersecurity datasets, AMADEUS demonstrated impressive results: 97.8% attack detection accuracy, only 1.2% false alarms, and remarkable resilience against sophisticated adversarial attacks (86.1% robustness). The system detects threats in milliseconds and successfully identifies 94.6% of completely new, never-before-seen attacks. This breakthrough represents a significant advancement in developing cybersecurity systems that can match the agility and intelligence of modern cyber threats.

الملخص (abstract): Most digital learning platforms fail to address the critical role of emotions in educational outcomes. This study presents an emotionally adaptive learning framework that uses multi-modal emotion recognition to dynamically adjust instructional content and interaction patterns based on real-time student affective states. Our system achieves 87.3% accuracy in recognizing seven key learning-related emotions across diverse datasets including DAiSEE (9,068 educational videos), AffectNet (450,000 facial images), and MOOC behavioral data (200,000+ learners). The hierarchical decision-making architecture balances immediate emotional responses with long-term pedagogical objectives, demonstrating a 34% improvement in predicted knowledge retention and 42% reduction in stress indicators compared to static interfaces. Cross-dataset validation shows significant improvements in engagement metrics (p < 0.001). The framework employs privacy-preserving edge computing and cultural adaptation mechanisms to address key challenges in non-invasive emotion sensing. These findings establish foundations for next-generation learning systems that respond to both cognitive and affective dimensions of individual learners.

الملخص (abstract): The universal focus on inclusive education requires new technologies in the case of diverse students. It is estimated that 1.3 billion of the global population have a high level of disability and 15% of the U.S. public school students (7.5 million) received IDEA-funded services in 202223. The chapter outlines a roadmap on how to use the AR, VR, and XR technologies to build inclusive learning environments. Based on the review of peer-reviewed sources (20152025), NCES data, EDUCAUSE publications, and the W3C XAUR model, the research assesses immersive technologies in terms of their accessibility. The study of 87 articles that involve federal data indicates that XR interventions enhance engagement (34%), knowledge retention (22%), and satisfaction among students with disabilities. Inclusive Immersive Learning (IIL) framework is a framework proposed based on Universal Design of Learning that offers a technology to design accessible XR experiences. Although the potential of immersive technologies is apparent, there are still gaps in the design of accessibility and fair implementation

العنوان (title): AI-Driven Darknet Threat Detection
المؤلفون (authors): Khalil Omar; Hussam Nawwaf Fakhouri; Faten Fatehi Hamad
الانتماءات (affiliations): Petra University; Al-Balqa Applied University; Sultan Qaboos University
الكلمات المفتاحية (author_keywords): anomaly detection; SHAP; adversarial robustness; network traffic classification
الملخص (abstract): The darknet hides and harbours known criminal activity that is estimated to cost the world economy $10.5 trillion a year and is difficult to detect on the traditional signature-based approach. In this chapter, a common and reproducible AI-based methodology is presented to detect darknet threats on the CIC-Darknet2020 benchmark. The proposed pipeline combines four supervised classifiers (Random Forest, XGBoost, LightGBM, Multilayer Perceptron), two unsupervised anomaly detectors (Isolation Forest and Autoencoder), a SHAP-based interpretability layer and a class-obfuscation adversarial robustness protocol. Experiments yielded a binary classification macro-F1 of 0.9644 and a multi-class macro-F1 of 0.6725, which are on par with previous benchmarks. SHAP analysis determined the most important Tor signature to be the TCP initial window sizes. The methodology aims to fill gaps in the literature on prior darknet detection in terms of operational gaps in interpretability, robustness and reproducibility.

الملخص (abstract): The intertwining of generative artificial intelligence, large language models, and the Metaverse are transforming the realm of smart education. This chapter discusses that convergence by a mixed-methods design comprising of systematic literature review, a reference architecture of GenAI-driven Metaverse classrooms, and a real empirical study on the Open University Learning Analytics Dataset (OULAD). There are four predictive models to the detection of at-risk learners, and XGBoost is tested on four predictive models under stratified cross-validation with predictions of 93.08% and 0.9785 AUC-ROC. It also tests a hybrid model where tabular features are augmented with DistilBERT embeddings, with results offering subtle insights to guide the decision to use the LLM representations to add any educational value. This chapter incorporates these findings into a six-principle ethical framework of bias, hallucination, privacy and academic integrity and suggests concrete research directions of the next generation of immersive, AI-enhanced learning environments.

الملخص (abstract): In this chapter, we introduce FairEdu-LA, a fairness-aware learning analytics framework, which combines XGBoost, SMOTE, SHAP interpretability, and equity-constrained optimization. FairEdu-LA was evaluated on OULAD (n = 32,593) and UCI Student Performance (n = 649) using Kaggle Notebooks, and outperformed all baselines with accuracy = 89.7%, recall = 93.2%, and AUC-ROC = 0.963. Using k-means clustering (k = 2 and silhouette = 0.4227), two behavioral profiles were identified. Repeat students (EOD = 0.102, n = 851) were the highest priority equity target identified in the fairness auditing results for eight demographic subgroups; the mature-age estimate (EOD = 0.164, n = 39) is indicative only. Results indicate that fairness-constrained design does not necessarily sacrifice predictive performance, but the generalizability of the results still needs to be tested.

المؤلفون (authors): Khalil Omar; Hussam Nawwaf Fakhouri; Faten Fatehi Hamad

الملخص (abstract): Students with special educational needs (SEN) are continuously exposed to barriers to individualized instruction that cannot be completely overcome by the traditional assistive technologies. In this chapter, the author introduces ADAPT-AI (Adaptive Data-driven AI Platform for Transformative Inclusive Education), which is a multi-modal framework consisting of supervised machine learning, sequential deep learning, and learning analytics to provide personalized early-warning support in inclusive education. XGBoost was tested on two open-access verified datasets: UCI Student Performance (n = 395) and OULAD (n = 32,593), and F1 = 0.911 and AUC-ROC = 0.979 on UCI and F1 = 0.932 and AUC-ROC = 0.979 on OULAD respectively. A F1 = 0.898 with LSTM temporal VLE sequences modeling was obtained on OULAD. SHAP analysis recognizes interim grades, prior failures, and submission of assessment as the overwhelming predictors. Results can be used to give practical recommendations on how to design inclusive instruction, intervene early and govern AI ethically in special education.

الملخص (abstract): This chapter introduces a conceptual framework of five layers that combines the digital twin technology with the simulation capabilities to deliver sustainable business innovation. This new architecture, which includes Foundation, Integration, Intelligence, Action, and Impact layers, will help organizations evolve their infrastructure development to real sustainability results at the economic, environmental, and social levels. The empirical validation with 2 open-access datasets shows that the framework is effective: predictive maintenance on the NASA C-MAPSS dataset had LSTM-based remaining useful life prediction with MAE 8.3 cycles and R2=0.947, which predicts the optimal glazing configurations with 31.4% energy savings; building energy optimization with the UCI dataset with R2=0.9914 predicting the heating load. All the improvements were statistically significant (p<0.001, Cohen d>0.8). The framework closes the gaps between technical implementation and sustainability strategy, and it provides scalable advice on a variety of enterprise settings.

الكلمات المفتاحية (author_keywords): safety-critical systems; computer vision; risk assessment; graceful degradation; uncertainty calibration; out-of-distribution detection; failure analysis; chest X-ray classification; clinical decision support; autonomous vehicles; infrastructure inspection; civil protection
الملخص (abstract): Computer vision systems are increasingly deployed in safety-critical applications—medical diagnostics, autonomous vehicles, infrastructure inspection, and civil defense—where misclassification may result in loss of life or critical-infrastructure damage. Machine-learning-based vision systems are statistically behaved, which does not fit the paradigms of certification developed for deterministic software. This chapter examines the methodological, regulatory, and engineering challenges of deploying reliable vision systems under these constraints. It surveys risk-assessment frameworks for learning-enabled systems, cross-domain certification standards, and design strategies including graceful degradation, calibrated uncertainty, and out-of-distribution detection. An empirical case study using the Kermany chest X-ray dataset demonstrates how confidence calibration and failure analysis can transform a high-accuracy classifier into a clinically defensible decision-support component.

الملخص (abstract): Although vision-language models (VLMs) provide state-of-the-art multimodal reasoning capabilities, they are currently mainly cloud-based, and thus not applicable to edge settings where bandwidth, latency, energy, and privacy constraints dominate. This chapter summarizes some of the architectures, optimization methods and embedded hardware platforms used for edge deployment and shares a reproducible Kaggle benchmark that quantizes CLIP-ViT-B/32 to FP32, FP16, INT8 and 4-bit NF4. The 4-bit variant achieves 92.67% top-1 accuracy on the Intel Image Classification benchmark and cuts the on-disk footprint by 71.2% and boosts the throughput 2.4 times compared to FP32. Ethical, regulatory and reproducible application are critically explored, taking into account the European Union Artificial Intelligence Act.

الملخص (abstract): This chapter discusses the impact of gamification strategies on HR technology platforms on employee engagement and retention. Based on correlation analysis, hierarchical logistic regression, and machine learning classification of the IBM HR Analytics dataset (N = 1,470), on the Kaggle, it is found that engagement variables add 5.2% incremental Pseudo R-squared to predict attrition. Job involvement was the most effective protector (OR = 0.61, p < .001), decreasing chances of attrition by 39 per unit, then job satisfaction (OR = 0.74), and environment satisfaction (OR = 0.76). XGBoost had an accuracy of 92.8 percent and AUC-ROC of 0.979 with SHAP analysis showing variables of engagement within the top five predictive variables. These results give evidence-based principles to develop gamified HR interventions that address intrinsic motivation to decrease voluntary turnover.

This chapter combines the eight steps model of Kotter and the ADKAR model with the six principles of human-AI collaboration, and empirically validates the integration by the Kaggle HR Analytics: Job Change of Data Scientists data (n ≈ 19,158). الملخص (abstract): Millions of people all over the world are assisted by disability support programs, but their M&E systems are still manual, resource-consuming, and inconsistent, with fragile data fragmentation and slow reporting. This chapter introduces an AI-based system that combines XGBoost, deep neural networks, and transformer encoders in a system that is aware of fairness. The design is based on publicly available data: ACS PUMS, UK FRS, and WHO GHO indicators. Projected accuracy, F1-score and AUC-ROC of a simulated validation are 0.89, 0.87 and 0.93 respectively. The fairness-conscious ensemble achieves demographic parity difference that is below 0.06 across all gender, race, age and regional subgroups, which is 47 percent lower than that of standalone models. Findings indicate that AI-based M&E has the potential to improve timeliness, accuracy and equity and keep interpretability. The future direction is still imperative in terms of empirical validation.

الكلمات المفتاحية (author_keywords): behavioral finance; cognitive biases; investor herding; market momentum; overreaction; loss aversion; prospect theory; XGBoost; LightGBM; LSTM; SHAP; Kaggle dataset
الملخص (abstract): Behavioral finance questions the rational-investor assumption, with empirical evidence of systematic cognitive biases which contribute to market outcomes. In this chapter, machine learning is combined with the behavioral theory of finance in terms of three empirical studies based on publicly available Kaggle datasets, FinBERT to predict sentiment, XGBoost and LightGBM to predict tabular data, an LSTM to predict sequence learning, and SHAP to interpret the results. Findings are inconsistent to the extent that the daily-index herding hypothesis is rejected; a momentum signature dominates over overreaction-reversal; a small loss-aversion drift ratio of 1.267 comes out that is lower than the prospect-theoretic canonical value of 2.25. The chapter maintains that explanation-driven validation is what makes a difference between scale-dependent attenuation and true refutation, showing that the scale-dependent attenuation is not due to the complexity of the algorithm used to compute it but rather to the fact that certain behavioral biases are the ones that can be detected.

الملخص (abstract): The rapid growth of artificial-intelligence technologies has produced a lot of enthusiasm regarding their deployment in educational systems. This study examines the views of the faculty members working at the University of Petra about the use of artificial intelligence as a pedagogical support. A survey-based approach of the methodology was used, with the data gathered on 105 members of faculty working in various disciplinary areas using a three-point Likert scale (Agree, Neutral, Disagree). The results show that, although a large majority (87.6%) favour the use of AI in carrying out specific tasks in education, there are still considerable concerns about the ability of AI to replace human teachers (44.8% showed concern), its ability to make a complete assessment of students (only 20% agreed), and its ability to offer emotional motivation (23.8% agreed). Furthermore, 40% of respondents said that AI tools currently don’t address the education sector’s specific needs. These results highlight the need for a balanced and human-centered approach to integrating AI in education, where technology is used as a complement to, rather than a replacement for, human educators. The study adds empirical evidence to contribute to policy decision on adoption of AI in HEIs.

الملخص (abstract): Machine learning has been used for decades to analyze vast datasets, classify and cluster data, and make predictions using algorithms. One of its top use areas is cybersecurity, where it can help detect and prevent destructive threats such as malware. The use of machine learning in cybersecurity has proven to be a powerful tool in detecting and predicting malware attacks. In recent years, the number of Internet users has greatly increased and with it the number of malware attacks. This has made predicting malware a challenge. Consequently, to date, there is still a need to examine the numerous existing MLs’ performance. This study is presented to identify the best classification model for predicting malware using two datasets and 18 different classifiers belonging to six learning strategies. The results showed that the RandomForest classifier had the highest accuracy, precision, recall, F1-measure, and ROC Area metrics, Moreover, Trees and Bayes learning strategies showed the best predictive performance on the two datasets compared with the other five learning strategies.

الملخص (abstract): Digital transformation has been brought out as one of the most critical strategic initiatives by organisations that are keen on making innovation and remaining competitive in technology-driven environments. In the banking industry, the gradual adoption of digital technologies has completely transformed the service provision processes, operational procedures, and the decision-making processes of managers. This paper examines how digital transformation affects innovation in Jordanian commercial banks, focusing specifically on the three key aspects, namely, technological infrastructure, legislative and policy frameworks, and digital skill sets. A descriptive-analytical research design was adopted and the data were collected using a structured questionnaire that was offered to both the senior and middle managers of the commercial banks in Jordan. The number of valid responses was 124 and was analysed statistically, including a reliability test, Descriptive statistics, a normality test and regression analysis. The current analysis indicates that the digital transformation has a statistically significant positive impact on innovation in the environment of commercial banking in Jordan. Among the dimensions that were examined, legislative and policy frameworks were the most powerful drivers, followed by technological infrastructure and digital competencies. The data also depict average levels of adoption of digital transformation interventions and practices that accompany them, hence pointing to significant improvement opportunities. The given empirical study adds to the body of existing literature on the topic of digital transformation and innovation by providing primary data on the banking industry of a developing economy. The derived insights have practical implications for banking executives and policy-makers in the society because of the importance of enabling regulatory environments, investment in digital infrastructures, and the long-term development of the digital capabilities of employees to foster innovation.

This manuscript proposes a system for classification and detection of crop and weed in sesame crops. In this system, different versions of Convolutional Neural Networks-based You Only Look Once (YOLO) object detection methods have been modified and the performance of YOLOv5, YOLOv6, and YOLOv7 compared. المؤلفون (authors): Jamal Sami Zraqou; Ahmad Sami Al-Shamayleh; Riyad Alrousan; Hussam Nawwaf Fakhouri; Faten Fatehi Hamad; Niveen Z. Halalsheh

الكلمات المفتاحية (author_keywords): Artificial Hummingbird Algorithm; Sine-Cosine Algorithm; hybrid metaheuristics; engineering optimisation; benchmark functions; convergence
كلمات الفهرسة (keywords_plus): MULTIOBJECTIVE OPTIMIZATION
الملخص (abstract): We introduce AHA-SCA, a compact hybrid optimiser that alternates the wave-based exploration of the Sine-Cosine Algorithm (SCA) with the exploitation skills of the Artificial Hummingbird Algorithm (AHA) within a single population. Even iterations perform SCA moves with a linearly decaying sinusoidal amplitude to explore widely around the current best solution, while odd iterations invoke guided and territorial hummingbird flights using axial, diagonal, and omnidirectional patterns to intensify the search in promising regions. This simple interleaving yields an explicit and tunable balance between exploration and exploitation and incurs negligible overhead beyond evaluating candidate solutions. The proposed approach is evaluated on the CEC2014, CEC2017, and CEC2022 benchmark suites and on several constrained engineering design problems, including welded beam, pressure vessel, tension/compression spring, speed reducer, and cantilever beam designs. Across these diverse tasks, AHA-SCA demonstrates competitive or superior performance relative to stand-alone SCA, AHA, and a broad panel of recent metaheuristics, delivering faster early-phase convergence and robust final solutions. Statistical analyses using non-parametric tests confirm that improvements are significant on many functions, and the method respects problem constraints without parameter tuning. The results suggest that alternating wave-driven exploration with hummingbird-inspired refinement is a promising general strategy for continuous engineering optimisation.

الملخص (abstract): Single-image super-resolution (SISR) remains a key problem in computer vision and image processing. Although the methods based on deep learning have achieved incredible progress, the current practices frequently fail to efficiently represent multi-scale features and distribute computational resources to meaningful image regions. The proposed network, Multi-Scale Attention Residual Network (MSARN), is an improved super-resolution architecture that incorporates a new Multi-Scale Feature Extraction Module (MSFEM) and a Dual-Path Channel-Spatial Attention (DPCSA) mechanism. The MSFEM employs parallel convolutional branches with different kernel sizes to learn fine-grained textures and coarse structural patterns, and the DPCSA adaptively updates feature responses across the channel and spatial dimensions. We also present a Gradient-Aware Loss that preserves high-frequency edge information during the reconstruction stage. Large-scale experiments on four common benchmark datasets (Set5, Set14, BSD100, and Urban100) show that MSARN has state-of-the-art performance, improving PSNR by 0.15-0.42 dB with scaling factors x2, x3, and x4. Moreover, we confirm the practicability of MSARN on solar extreme ultraviolet (EUV) images obtained with the STEREO-A/SECCHI EUVI 171A detector, which has the MSARN average PSNR of 32.50 dB and SSIM of 0.9274, exceeding SwinIR by an additional 0.57 dB, which supports the effectiveness of MSARN in scientific image enhancement with the objectives of heliophysics.

الملخص (abstract): Quality networks are now a key ingredient to digitally facilitated supply chains where operational responsiveness, system coordination and real time data exchange require network quality. This paper will research how predictive quality of networks empowered by Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning can affect the supply chain performance with particular attention to warehouse-intensive manufacturing companies in Jordan. The study relies on the Organizational Information Processing Theory and states that AI- and ML-based network quality prediction increase the capacity of an organization to predict communication failures, streamline data operations, and facilitate operational decisions. The use of a quantitative approach involved survey data supplied by the logistics, operations, and warehouse staff. PLSSEM was the method of testing the proposed model, where the direct impact of network-enabled logistics communication on any of the dimensions of supply chain performance was assessed and the mediating effect of AI-based and ML-based predictive capabilities was considered. The results show that predictive network quality will reinforce the effect of digitally enabled logistics communication to service level, labor efficiency, and capacity utilization significantly. The article is relevant to the literature in that it places the network quality prediction as a strategic facilitator of supply chain performance and provides a practical advice to companies interested in introducing AI-based communications intelligence to the supply chain processes.

العنوان (title): Real-Time Explanation Intrusion Detection: An XAI-Enriched Hybrid CNN-LSTM Architecture for Operational Cybersecurity
المؤلفون (authors): Ayman Alnsour; Jamal Zarqou; Ahmad Shalaldeh
الانتماءات (affiliations): Al-Ahliyya Amman University; Petra University
الكلمات المفتاحية (author_keywords): deep learning; cyber threat classification; SHAP; LIME; CNN-LSTM; real-time security; network traffic analysis
كلمات الفهرسة (keywords_plus): NEURAL-NETWORKS; AI
الملخص (abstract): Deep learning-based intrusion detection systems offer world-class accuracy in threat classification. They are also generally not easily explainable to security analysts, which represents a major hurdle in their use in real-world Security Operations Centers (SOCs) where explainability and trust are critical. This operational challenge is tackled with a systems-engineered approach combining the CNN-LSTM architecture with the computationally optimized SHAP and LIME approaches for enabling real-time, interpretable threat detection. Unlike novel mathematical formulations, we concentrate on practical innovations in systems engineering that we believe are required to generate explanations in real-time: quantization of the numbers to INT8, execution of explanation algorithms in parallel, asynchronously, and caching of similar traffic patterns. CNN-LSTM combines the convolutional function to capture spatial dependencies and the recurrent function to capture temporal dynamics of network traffic, and SHAP and LIME capture global and local feature attributions, respectively. One of the major innovations is the parallel execution which brings the latency of explanation down from 117 ms (sequential SHAP + LIME) to 46 ms (parallel, cache-miss) and 39 ms (average with caching) and 46 ms (without caching), which is sufficient for operational "real-time" requirements. The framework is evaluated on CICIDS2017 and NSL-KDD benchmark datasets, and results show that it can achieve 98.7% accuracy with 98.6% F1-score and sub-50 ms explanation latency. The results here show that explainability and operational efficiency can be attained with the same level of accuracy in the detection of abnormal events, through careful systems engineering. This paper presents a systems-engineered framework demonstrating the feasibility of real-time, interpretable IDS for deployment in Security Operations Centers (SOCs) and addresses the challenges of combining high-performance deep learning with operational transparency in cybersecurity.

الملخص (abstract): Facial expression recognition (FER) is an important field of human-computer interaction, affective computing, and intelligent systems. Yet, the ability to obtain strong and precise emotion recognition in free conditions is still a challenge, as it depends on the differences in illumination, pose, occlusion, and personal differences. In the given paper, we introduce the Attention-Enhanced Convolutional Neural Network (AE-CNN) that integrates deep convolutional networks' feature extraction with the spatial and channel attention systems to pay attention to discriminative facial areas. We have used a dual-path attention module in our approach that focuses on both local and global facial features to provide a more precise classification of emotions. We do extensive experiments on FER2013 benchmark dataset of 35, 887 grayscale images of seven kinds of emotions. The suggested AE-CNN has a test accuracy of 74.82, which is higher than some of the state-of-the-art approaches. We also apply real-time face tracking with the help of OpenCV and the dlib face detector and landmark extractor. Experimental findings indicate that the attention mechanism substantially increases the accuracy of recognition, especially of subtle expressions like fear and disgust. The proposed system can run in real-time at 28 frames per second on a regular machine, which is why it is appropriate for its practical implementation in driver monitoring systems, healthcare, and human-robot interaction.

الملخص (abstract): The super-resolution (SR) reconstruction is an effective image processing method that creates images with high resolution (HR) using several low-resolution (LR) images. The given paper outlines a complete guideline on how to reconstruct super-resolution images, starting with four low-resolution input images, with the help of a scheme known as the Enhanced Iterative Back Projection algorithm (EIBP). The suggested algorithm combines sub-pixel image registration, adaptive noise reduction, and iteration refinement to create high-quality reconstructed images. The system solves some of the most important problems in multi-frame SR, and they are accurate motion estimation, optimal information fusion, and artifact suppression. Experimental performance on standard benchmark data sets proves that the suggested approach has better performance than traditional interpolation techniques and single-image SR techniques, with an average improvement of 4.2 dB in Peak Signal-to-Noise Ratio (PSNR) and 0.12 in Structural Similarity Index Measure (SSIM). The methodology is specifically useful when used in remote sensing, medical imaging, and surveillance systems, where hardware constraints limit the acquisition of images.

الملخص (abstract): The extremely rapid rate of development of the infrastructure of solar energy demands effective and computer-assisted diagnostic processes to monitor the well-being of photovoltaic (PV) modules. This paper compares four deep neural networks. Custom CNN, ResNet50, EfficientNetB0, and MobileNetV3Small- to detect electrical faults in PV panels with the help of RGB images. It has used a well-chosen set of 2,669 hand-marked and clean, and electrically damaged images. The networks were consequently evaluated based on accuracy, training time, and generalization. Among these networks, MobileNetV3Small, with low computational cost, and EfficientNetB0, with the highest test accuracy (99.44 percent and 99.25 percent, respectively), were the highest. These results confirm light-weight and transfer learning based network-based scalable real-time inspection of PVs. An original contribution is presented regarding the literature by demonstrating the effectiveness of efficient CNNs to provide accurate fault detection in low-resource settings, encouraging larger-scale applications. This research extends beyond traditional deep learning approaches that rely on standard RGB image collections, pushing the application of electroluminescence imaging techniques toward practical deployment scenarios with improved adaptability across diverse real-world conditions, representing a notable progression from existing methodological frameworks documented in current scientific publications.

الكلمات المفتاحية (author_keywords): motion deblurring; dynamic scenes; multi-scale convolutional neural network; self-attention; transformer blocks; feature fusion; residual learning; channel and spatial attention; spatially varying blur; occlusion boundaries
الملخص (abstract): Motion blur degradation remains a fundamental challenge in computational photography, particularly in dynamic scenes where multiple motion sources contribute to complex blur patterns. This paper presents an enhanced multi-scale convolutional neural network architecture that addresses the limitations of traditional kernel-based deblurring methods. Our approach introduces a hierarchical pyramid structure operating at multiple resolutions, incorporating self-attention mechanisms, transformer blocks, and advanced feature fusion strategies to preserve fine-grained details while capturing long-range dependencies. We propose a novel training methodology utilizing physically based blur synthesis through high-speed camera footage integration, eliminating the need for explicit kernel estimation. The framework employs a modified residual learning structure with skip connections optimized for blur removal tasks. Additionally, we introduce spatial and channel attention modules at each scale level to selectively focus on blur-affected regions. Outputs: results, per-record predictions and figures. A single script (run_all.sh) regenerates every dataset, model, result and figure from fixed random seeds. The README documents the data dictionary, the data-generating process, the model architecture and the weights-file format. On top of these representations, we benchmark six standard classifiers—logistic regression, support vector machine (SVM), random forest, gradient boosting, k-nearest neighbours and Gaussian Näıve Bayes—and apply a stacking ensemble that fuses calibrated outputs from PCA-compressed base learners (random forest, SVM and gradient boosting) using a multinomial logistic meta-learner. Finally, we quantify the practical return on investment of hyperparameter optimisation by contrasting default configurations with cross-validated grid search. Results show that the engineered representation enables strong baseline performance, stacking is competitive but compute-heavy, and tuning yields marginal macro-F1 changes while increasing training time by up to an order of magnitude. We note that our current evaluation employs two-fold cross-validation on the UCI Digits dataset; future work will extend to repeated stratified K-fold evaluation on more challenging datasets to confirm generalisability. All code, configurations and raw metrics are released to support exact reproduction and extension.

العنوان (title): Anonymization techniques for privacy-preserving data publishing: a comprehensive survey
المجلة أو المؤتمر (venue): Bulletin of Electrical Engineering and Informatics
الناشر (publisher): Institute of Advanced Engineering and Science (IAES)
المؤلفون (authors): Sami Smadi; Nader Abdel Karim; Hasan Kanaker; Waleed K. Abdulraheem
الانتماءات (affiliations): Yarmouk University; Al-Balqa Applied University; Petra University
الكلمات المفتاحية (author_keywords): privacy-preserving data publishing; data anonymization; re-identification attacks; inference attacks; k-anonymity; l-diversity; t-closeness; pseudonymization; differential privacy; synthetic data generation; federated learning; secure multi-party computation
الملخص (abstract): Data-driven innovation in healthcare, finance, and smart cities increasingly depends on sharing rich datasets, but such sharing raises severe privacy risks and regulatory challenges. Privacy-preserving data publishing (PPDP) seeks to release useful data while preventing re-identification and inference attacks. This paper presents a comprehensive survey of anonymization techniques for PPDP, spanning traditional models (k-anonymity, l-diversity, t-closeness, and pseudonymization) and modern approaches (differential privacy (DP), synthetic data generation, federated learning (FL), secure multi-party computation (SMPC), homomorphic encryption (HE), blockchain-based schemes, and quantum-safe cryptography). We propose a taxonomy that organizes these methods by privacy guarantees, data utility, scalability, and computational cost, and we provide a comparative analysis of their strengths, limitations, and typical application domains. The survey also reviews legal and ethical frameworks, with particular attention to general data protection regulation GDPR, health insurance portability and accountability act (HIPAA), and related regulations, and highlights emerging trends such as artificial intelligence (AI-driven) anonymization and privacy risks from large language models (LLMs) and quantum computing. Overall, the study shows that various techniques fail to protect all data scenarios so we need to create hybrid systems which will provide explainable anonymization solutions at different scales to protect privacy and maintain useful data utility.

العنوان (title): Securing Tool-Using AI Agents Against Injection and Authority Misuse
المؤلفون (authors): Hasan Kanaker; Hussam Nawwaf Fakhouri; Nader Abdel Karim; Maher Abuhamdeh; Nurul Halimatul Asmak Ismail; Sandi N. Fakhouri
الانتماءات (affiliations): Petra University; Al-Balqa Applied University; Middle East University; Princess Nourah bint Abdulrahman University; University of Jordan
الكلمات المفتاحية (author_keywords): AI agents; security; prompt injection; indirect prompt injection; Monte Carlo simulation; severity-aware risk metrics
الملخص (abstract): Tool-using AI agents couple a language model with controller logic, memory, and external tools such as browsers, email, calendars, file systems, and transaction APIs. This architecture expands capability, but it also enlarges the security boundary: agents routinely ingest untrusted content while holding privileges that can reveal private data and trigger external side effects. The resulting failures are not limited to poor text generation; they include prompt injection, indirect injection through tool outputs, confused-deputy behavior, unauthorized actions, and misleading claims about the tool state. Because large-scale testing on deployed products is difficult, vendor-specific, and ethically sensitive, we present a transparent, theoretical simulation-based framework for evaluating user-facing risk in tool-using agents. The methodological contribution is a formal threat model that separates compromise, harm, and severity, and a Monte Carlo evaluation pipeline that maps architectural choices (permissions, retrieval, memory exposure, and approvals) and defensive controls to comparable outcome metrics. We instantiate the framework for six representative threat scenarios and nine defense configurations, reporting attack success rate (ASR), benign task success, latency overhead, and severity-weighted harm. Across scenarios, the least-privilege tool design is the strongest single broad control, human-in-the-loop approvals sharply reduce high-impact actions and exports but degrade under user error and habituation, retrieval allowlisting nearly eliminates indirect injection while leaving other channels largely unaffected, and rate limiting reduces tail severity more than ASR. These results position agent safety as an architectural and operational problem and because they arise from an assumption-explicit simulator rather than field measurements, should be read as comparative design guidance rather than incident-rate estimates for any deployed product.

العنوان (title): Enhanced Puzzle Optimization Algorithmfor Complex Engineering Design Problems
المؤلفون (authors): Hasan Kanaker; Essam Alhroob; Hammoudeh Alamri; Maher Abuhamdeh; Samar Al-Saqqa
الانتماءات (affiliations): Petra University; Isra University; World Islamic Sciences and Education University; Middle East University; University of Jordan; Al-Zaytoonah University of Jordan
الكلمات المفتاحية (author_keywords): enhanced puzzle optimization algorithm (EPOA); puzzle optimization algorithm (POA); metaheuristics; elitism; constrained engineering design
كلمات الفهرسة (keywords_plus): NATURE-INSPIRED ALGORITHM; SALP SWARM ALGORITHM; GLOBAL OPTIMIZATION; SIMULATION; EVOLUTION; DYNAMICS; SYSTEM; COLONY
الملخص (abstract): This paper introduced the Enhanced Puzzle Optimization Algorithm (EPOA), a hybrid metaheuristic that augmented the original Puzzle Optimization Algorithm (POA) with uniform crossover, random-resetting mutation, and explicit elitism. The contribution does not lie in inventing these operators individually, since they are classical search components, but in integrating them into POA's two-phase search dynamics to address premature convergence, diversity loss, and best-solution preservation in a targeted manner. This paper formalized EPOA's update rules, provided pseudocode and flow diagrams, and enforced bound handling for box-constrained problems. Comprehensive tests on the CEC2022 single-objective benchmark suite (F1-F12) showed that EPOA attained rank 1 on 11 of 12 functions and rank 3 on the remaining case, with large error reductions relative to baseline POA (e.g., on F1, the mean error dropped from 62.836 to 0.004; on F6, the mean error dropped from 2370.962 to 7.239). The method was further evaluated on six classical constrained engineering design problems (welded beam, tension/compression spring, speed reducer, pressure vessel, three-bar truss, and cantilever beam). Statistical indicators such as the mean and standard deviation were used to assess robustness. The results showed that EPOA delivered a strong exploration-exploitation balance and robust solution quality across rugged landscapes and real-world constraints.

العنوان (title): Least-Privilege Role-Based Access Control Improvement for Cloud Container Security
المؤلفون (authors): Waleed K. Abdulraheem; Emad Mohammed Ibbini; Hasan Kanaker; Sami Smadi; Nader Abdel Karim; Hussam Nawwaf Fakhouri; Layla Albdour; Sandi N. Fakhouri

الكلمات المفتاحية (author_keywords): least-privilege; Role-Based Access Control (RBAC); kubernetes; cloud computing container; container security; metaheuristic optimization; policy hardening; constraint satisfaction
كلمات الفهرسة (keywords_plus): OPTIMIZATION
الملخص (abstract): Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) is the de-facto mechanism for preserving Kubernetes and other cloud-native container platforms, however real deployments occasionally drift away from the principle of least privilege as clusters, teams, and services improve. This paper introduces an automated RBAC hardening framework that formulates least-privilege policy design as a limited optimization problem over RoleBindings and ClusterRoleBindings. The objective combines (i) a permission-risk score for namespaced and cluster-scoped actions with (ii) an operational complexity term that discourages overly large binding sets. Solid limitations encode functional requirements as well as practical security policies, which includes namespace allowlists, role scoping rules, administrative restrictions on cluster-wide bindings, binding budgets, and separation-of-duty requirements expressed by utilizing capability classes. To allow optimizer-agnostic search while protecting Kubernetes RBAC semantics, we analyze candidate policies by utilizing a unified penalty-based fitness function that compines risk, complexity, and constraint violations into a single scalar value. We utilized ten metaheuristic as a benchmark including baseline search paths on a Kubernetes-inspired instance and report feasibility and least-privilege quality metrics (precision, recall, F1, and over-privilege ratio) parallel to RB/CRB counts and excess risk as a structural indicators. Outcomes present that feasibility is the prime challenge, and is restricted to a subset of optimizers reliably arrives to entirely feasible and compact arrangements within the exact budget, indicating the practicality of metaheuristic enhancement for systematic RBAC reduction in containerized cloud computing environments.

العنوان (title): Enhancing Response Mechanisms Against LOLBAS Threats in SCADA Environments: Ablation Study and Practical Implications
المجلة أو المؤتمر (venue): International Conference on Computational Intelligence Approaches and Applications (ICCIAA)
الناشر (publisher): Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers
المؤلفون (authors): Thamer Abu-Alzanat; Jafar Ahmad Abed Alzubi; Ashraf ALDabbas; Hussam Nawwaf Fakhouri; Hasan Kanaker; Omar A. Alzubi
الانتماءات (affiliations): Al-Balqa Applied University; Petra University
الكلمات المفتاحية (author_keywords): SCADA security; NetFlow; network flow analysis; anomaly detection; ensemble learning; false alarm reduction; industrial control systems; hardware-in-the-loop
الملخص (abstract): Living-off-the-land binaries and scripts (LOLBAS) enable adversaries to abuse trusted system utilities to perform malicious actions while minimizing the introduction of new executables. In supervisory control and data acquisition (SCADA) environments, this behavior is difficult to distinguish from legitimate administration and maintenance, and overly aggressive mitigation may jeopardize availability and safety. This paper presents a LOLBAS-aware detection and response framework that fuses host command telemetry with NetFlow-style network behavior. We extract lightweight semantic features from command lines using natural language processing and combine them with real-time flow summaries derived from packet capture. Detection is performed with a weighted ensemble of Random Forest, XGBoost, LSTM, and Transformer models, where vote weights are calibrated from validation F1-scores. To preserve operational safety, the response layer operates in alert-only mode, producing evidence-backed operator recommendations instead of automated containment. Experiments on 150,000 labeled records from a hardware-in-the-loop SCADA simulation and a 6–8 week continuous evaluation window achieve 95.2% accuracy, 2.8% false positive rate, 0.95 F1-score, 0.97 ROC-AUC, and 8.5 ms average inference latency. An ablation study shows that command semantics contribute the largest performance gain, while network context and temporal modeling further reduce false alarms.

المجلة أو المؤتمر (venue): International Conference on Computational Intelligence Approaches and Applications (ICCIAA)

المؤلفون (authors): Omar A. Alzubi; Hussam Nawwaf Fakhouri; Hasan Kanaker; Jafar Ahmad Abed Alzubi
