الكلمات المفتاحية (author_keywords): biometric authentication; decision threshold selection; false acceptance rate; false rejection rate; metaheuristic optimization; swarm intelligence; Harris Hawks Optimization; grey wolf optimizer; whale optimization algorithm; cost minimization
الملخص (abstract): Selecting an appropriate decision threshold is critical in biometric verification because the false acceptance rate (FAR) and false rejection rate (FRR) trade off against each other. This paper formulates threshold selection as a cost minimization problem and compares a suite of metaheuristic algorithms against an exhaustive grid search. Ten recent swarm-based optimizers—Harris Hawks optimization (HHO), slime mould algorithm (SMA), manta ray foraging optimization (MRFO), grey wolf optimizer (GWO), whale optimization algorithm (WOA), sine–cosine algorithm (SCA), hunger games search (HGS), northern goshawk optimization (NGO), white shark optimizer (WSO) and golden jackal optimization (GJO)—are evaluated on synthetic score distributions. Each algorithm runs for 300 iterations and additional performance metrics including accuracy, balanced accuracy, F1 score, sensitivity, specificity and precision are reported. Convergence curves, bar charts and scatter plots visualise the results. The findings indicate that most metaheuristics converge rapidly to the optimal threshold found by grid search and achieve comparable performance, while runtime differences are minor. The paper provides a comprehensive comparison and discusses the strengths and limitations of each algorithm for threshold tuning in biometric systems.

العنوان (title): Differentially Private Intrusion Detection for Multi-Tenant Clouds via Objective-Perturbation Logistic Regression
المجلة أو المؤتمر (venue): International Conference on Computational Intelligence Approaches and Applications (ICCIAA)
الناشر (publisher): Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers
المؤلفون (authors): Omar A. Alzubi; Hussam Nawwaf Fakhouri; Hasan Kanaker; Jafar Ahmad Abed Alzubi
الانتماءات (affiliations): Al-Balqa Applied University; Petra University
الكلمات المفتاحية (author_keywords): differential privacy; intrusion detection; multi-tenant cloud; privacy-utility trade-off; NSL-KDD dataset; privacy-preserving machine learning
الملخص (abstract): Cloud intrusion detection systems (IDS) increasingly rely on centralized machine learning over network-flow and connection telemetry aggregated across tenants. While centralization improves coverage and detection quality, it also creates privacy risks: adversaries with access to trained models or prediction APIs can infer whether a specific tenant record (e.g., a connection attempt) participated in training, or can extract sensitive statistical signals about rare behaviors. We present a fully reproducible experimental study of pure ε-differential privacy (DP) training for binary intrusion detection using objective-perturbation logistic regression. Our artifact implements an end-to-end pipeline (dataset download, integrity checks, preprocessing, training, evaluation, tables, and publication-quality figures) and compares a DP logistic regression model (DP-LR) against non-private baselines (LR, Random Forest, HistGradientBoosting) on the NSL-KDD benchmark. We report standard IDS metrics (Accuracy, Precision, Recall, F1, ROC-AUC, PR-AUC), runtime, and DP parameters, and quantify the privacy–utility tradeoff through an ε sweep. All quantitative results and figures in this manuscript are generated by the accompanying codebase.

العنوان (title): SecEdgeOpt: Risk-Aware Joint Optimization of Secure Task Offloading and Intrusion-Detection Placement in Multi-Access Edge Computing
المجلة أو المؤتمر (venue): International Conference on Computational Intelligence Approaches and Applications (ICCIAA)
الناشر (publisher): Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers
المؤلفون (authors): Hasan Kanaker; Faten Fatehi Hamad; Hazem Abu-Adaiq
الانتماءات (affiliations): Petra University; Sultan Qaboos University; Applied Science Private University
الكلمات المفتاحية (author_keywords): mobile edge computing; risk-aware optimization; mixed-integer nonlinear programming; hybrid metaheuristic; differential evolution; particle swarm optimization; end-to-end delay; energy consumption; Internet of Things security
الملخص (abstract): Multi-access edge computing (MEC) reduces latency by moving computation closer to users, but it also enlarges the attack surface by distributing resources across heterogeneous and often lightly managed edge sites. This paper studies a joint security–performance optimization problem in which (i) mobile/IoT tasks must be assigned to local execution, one of multiple edge servers, or a cloud fallback; (ii) each task selects a security level (e.g., encryption strength) that trades computational overhead for risk reduction; and (iii) each edge server may activate a lightweight intrusion detection system (IDS) instance with limited inspection capacity and operational cost. We formulate a mixed-integer nonlinear program that minimizes a weighted sum of end-to-end latency, energy consumption, and expected breach loss under bandwidth, CPU, and deadline constraints. To solve the resulting nonconvex combinatorial problem at practical scales, we propose SecEdgeOpt, a hybrid metaheuristic that combines differential evolution exploration with particle-swarm-inspired exploitation and a constraint-aware repair operator. evaluation on MEC scenarios shows that SecEdgeOpt achieves consistently lower composite cost than common optimizers (GA, PSO, DE, and GWO), with faster convergence and improved feasibility rates.

العنوان (title): Constraint-Aware Hybrid Metaheuristic Optimization for Joint IDS Placement and Key-Refresh Scheduling in Resource-Constrained IoT Edge Networks
المجلة أو المؤتمر (venue): International Conference on Computational Intelligence Approaches and Applications (ICCIAA)
الناشر (publisher): Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers
المؤلفون (authors): Hasan Kanaker; Samer A. B. Awwad
الانتماءات (affiliations): Petra University; Imam Mohammad ibn Saud Islamic University
الكلمات المفتاحية (author_keywords): resource-constrained networks; hybrid metaheuristic; binary particle swarm optimization; differential evolution; mixed-integer nonlinear programming; key management; security risk reduction; benchmark generator
الملخص (abstract): Security controls in Internet-of-Things (IoT) deployments must operate under tight energy, memory, and latency budgets, making how and where security is enforced an optimization problem rather than a fixed design choice. This paper formulates a joint IoT security optimization that selects (i) the placement of lightweight intrusion detection system (IDS) agents on edge nodes and (ii) per-device cryptographic key-refresh periods, while assigning devices to deployed IDS agents under capacity and distance constraints. The resulting mixed-integer nonlinear program is NP-hard due to combinatorial placement/assignment and nonlinear risk/overhead terms. To solve it, we propose a constraint-aware hybrid optimizer (CHPDE) that couples binary particle swarm optimization (BPSO) for placement with differential evolution (DE) operators for continuous key-refresh variables and a repair mechanism for feasibility. Using a synthetic IoT-edge benchmark generator, we provide theoretical performance tables and plots comparing genetic algorithm (GA), PSO, DE, and grey wolf optimizer (GWO) against CHPDE. Theoretical results indicate that CHPDE converges faster and achieves lower objective values with improved security-risk reduction under the same compute budget.

العنوان (title): A Hybrid NIZKP and Schnorr’s Protocol-Based Two-Factor Authentication for Secure and Scalable Healthcare Systems
المجلة أو المؤتمر (venue): International Conference on Computational Intelligence Approaches and Applications (ICCIAA)
الناشر (publisher): Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers
المؤلفون (authors): Bara’a O. Ghananim; Omar A. Alzubi; Wafa’ Za’al Alma’aitah; Hussam Nawwaf Fakhouri; Hasan Kanaker; Jafar Ahmad Abed Alzubi
الانتماءات (affiliations): Al-Balqa Applied University; Petra University
الكلمات المفتاحية (author_keywords): non-interactive zero-knowledge proofs; two-factor authentication; health information systems; role-based access control; one-time password; biometric authentication; authentication latency; privacy-preserving authentication
الملخص (abstract): Healthcare information systems increasingly rely on networked access to electronic health records and clinical services, making authentication latency and usability as critical as cryptographic strength. This paper presents a lightweight hybrid authentication framework that combines Schnorr identification with a Fiat-Shamir-derived non-interactive zero-knowledge proof (NIZKP), integrates a conventional second factor (OTP and/or biometric), and enforces role-based access control (RBAC). The design eliminates transmission of reusable password secrets during routine logins, keeps proof material constant-size, and targets fast verification suitable for high-throughput hospital gateways. We implement the pipeline and evaluate it under three simulated clinical traffic patterns aligned with eICU-inspired workload modeling: low traffic (50 users), high traffic (500 users), and burst peak load (100 users). Across scenarios, the end-to-end authentication time remains stable between 0.0107 s and 0.0109 s and stays below a 0.02 s benchmark. Reliability remains high, with success rates of 100.0%, 99.8%, and 99.0%; observed failures stem from injected OTP-expiry or biometric-mismatch events rather than cryptographic verification errors. These results suggest that Schnorr-style NIZKP authentication can provide privacy-preserving, scalable access control for healthcare environments when combined with practical 2FA and RBAC enforcement.

العنوان (title): Cost–Sensitive Phishing URL Detection for Cloud Email Gateways
المجلة أو المؤتمر (venue): International Conference on Computational Intelligence Approaches and Applications (ICCIAA)

المؤلفون (authors): Faten Fatehi Hamad; Hussam Nawwaf Fakhouri; Hasan Kanaker; Omar A. Alzubi
الانتماءات (affiliations): Sultan Qaboos University; Al-Balqa Applied University; Petra University
الكلمات المفتاحية (author_keywords): phishing URL detection; cost-sensitive classification; false positive reduction; logistic regression; security operations center; email security
الملخص (abstract): Phishing remains a persistent threat to cloud email and web gateways, enabling credential theft, fraud, and reputational harm. Modern security operations centres (SOCs) must triage large volumes of automated detections and therefore benefit from machine–learning (ML) models that not only detect attacks reliably but also keep false positives low to avoid analyst overload. This paper presents a fully study on phishing URL detection using a public dataset of 2015 URLs described by 16 lightweight engineered features. We benchmark four common classifiers and introduce a cost–sensitive logistic regression whose decision threshold is optimised to explicitly trade off false alarms against missed attacks. Our end–to–end pipeline covers data loading, preprocessing, model training, repeated stratified cross–validation, threshold calibration, and publication–quality visualisations. Across cross–validated experiments, the proposed approach reaches a precision of 0.98 while maintaining acceptable recall, illustrating that simple cost–aware thresholding can materially reduce alert load without increasing model complexity. All code, data, and experiment artefacts are released to support replication and extension.

المؤلفون (authors): Zaid Momani; Abidalrahman Moh’d; Shadi Shehadeh
الانتماءات (affiliations): Petra University; Eastern Illinois University; UT Quality,Edmonton,Canada
الكلمات المفتاحية (author_keywords): solar irradiance forecasting; weather data integration; attention-based LSTM; CNN-LSTM; hybrid deep learning model; missing data imputation
الملخص (abstract): Accurate solar irradiance forecasting is critical for optimizing renewable energy production, grid stability, and operational planning in regions with high solar potential. This paper presents a comprehensive system integrating large-scale weather data processing with hybrid deep learning models for solar irradiance prediction in high-irradiance regions. We develop two hybrid architectures: an Attention-LSTM model incorporating multi-head self-attention mechanisms, and a 1D CNN-LSTM model combining convolutional feature extraction with sequential learning. The system employs Hadoop-based distributed computing for efficient processing of multi-source weather data, including on-site measurements and satellite-derived information. Performance evaluation using real-world data from a solar installation demonstrates that both models achieve competitive accuracy for 10-minute ahead forecasting, with the Attention-LSTM model attaining 9.79% Mean Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE), superior to vanilla LSTM baselines (typically 15-25% MAPE) and competitive with state-of-the-art attention-enhanced methods. The complete system architecture addresses practical deployment challenges including data integration, missing value imputation, and scalable infrastructure for operational forecasting. Case studies demonstrate the system’s applicability for energy loss detection and operational efficiency optimization, achieving 12% improvement in energy utilization through prediction-driven scheduling.

العنوان (title): An AI-Driven Decision Support Framework for Change Order Management in Construction Projects: A Systematic Bibliometric Review
المجلة أو المؤتمر (venue): International Conference on Computational Intelligence Approaches and Applications (ICCIAA)
الناشر (publisher): Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers

الانتماءات (affiliations): Petra University; Universiti Teknologi MARA System; Universiti Teknologi MARA
الكلمات المفتاحية (author_keywords): Artificial Intelligence; Bibliometric Analysis; Change Order Management; Construction Projects; Decision Support Systems; Machine Learning
الملخص (abstract): Change orders—formal modifications to construction contracts that alter scope, cost, or schedule—represent persistent sources of delay, cost escalation, and dispute risk. This paper presents a bibliometric and thematic review examining how Artificial Intelligence (AI) is being integrated into decision support for change order management. Analysis of 122 Scopus-indexed publications (2019–2026) reveals that while 53% of research focuses on predictive analytics, only 7% addresses structured decision support, and governance integration—critical because change orders are legally binding contract modifications requiring formal authorisation—is notably absent from the literature. Building on this evidence, we propose a four-layer conceptual framework integrating established predictive capabilities with novel contributions: a Decision Translation Layer converting predictions into actionable recommendations, and a Governance Integration Layer ensuring contractual compliance through approval routing, stakeholder coordination, and audit mechanisms. The governance layer addresses a fundamental gap: AI recommendations cannot execute without mechanisms ensuring proper authorisation and documentation. This framework bridges the research-practice disconnect, advancing explainable, governance-aligned AI support for change order management in construction.

العنوان (title): Rethinking AI Ethics in Education: From Restrictive Policies to Learning-Oriented Design
المجلة أو المؤتمر (venue): International Conference on Computational Intelligence Approaches and Applications (ICCIAA)
الناشر (publisher): Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers
المؤلفون (authors): Suhailah Mohamed Noor; Zaid Momani
الانتماءات (affiliations): Universiti Teknologi MARA; Petra University
الكلمات المفتاحية (author_keywords): AI ethics in education; generative AI; AI policy in education; assessment integrity; moral reasoning; prompt chaining; human-in-the-loop; learning design; process-oriented assessment; critical thinking; metacognition; ethical AI use
الملخص (abstract): The rapid adoption of generative artificial intelligence in education has prompted many institutions to adopt restrictive policies framing AI ethics as compliance and control. While aiming to protect assessment integrity, such approaches risk limiting learning opportunities and fail to cultivate students’ ethical judgment. This conceptual paper argues that AI ethics in education should be reconceptualized as a pedagogical issue rather than purely regulatory. Drawing on learning design and process-oriented assessment principles, we develop Prompt Chaining with Human-in-the-Loop as a structured pedagogical methodology for cultivating ethical AI use. Prompt Chaining is conceptualized as a cognitive practice promoting iterative questioning, critical evaluation, and intellectual responsibility through structured, multi-step interactions. Human-in-the-Loop functions as the integrated oversight mechanism ensuring human judgment and accountability remain central throughout the learning process. By embedding ethical reasoning into everyday learning activities, this approach shifts discourse from restriction to learning and from compliance to responsibility, offering educators a pedagogically grounded pathway for fostering ethical AI use aligned with critical thinking, metacognition, and lifelong learning.

العنوان (title): Parametric FEM Study and Full-Scale Testing of Hole-Spanning Capacity in Spray Applied Pipe Linings
المؤلفون (authors): Ehsan Rajaie; Kawalpreet Kaur; Mohammad Najafi; Zaid Momani; Sanaz Ghalambor
الانتماءات (affiliations): University of North Texas; The University of Texas at Arlington
الكلمات المفتاحية (author_keywords): pipe rehabilitation; internal pressure; hydrostatic testing; steel pipes; parametric study; finite element model validation
الملخص (abstract): Polymeric Spray Applied Pipe Lining (SAPL) is a growing solution for rehabilitating pipelines with corrosion, leakage, and defects. It applies a polymeric liner to the pipe's interior, creating a barrier to handle pressure and extend service life; however, structural guidance for hole spanning under conservative non-bonded conditions remains limited. This paper develops and validates a 3D finite element model to evaluate liner performance under 500 psi internal pressure and then applies the model in a parametric study. Full-scale hydrostatic tests on 30-in. steel pipe specimens with 4- and 6-in. circular holes lined with polyurea liners (0.45–0.55 in. thickness) are used for FEM validation using measured liner strains. However, it also expands the attack surface: motion data can uniquely identify users, digital twins linking physical and virtual systems introduce vulnerabilities across multiple layers, and 6G networks will connect billions of devices requiring sub-millisecond security decisions. This chapter examines how latency, scalability and attack resilience can be balanced in immersive systems.

The chapter explores how real-time AI enables faster and more accurate decisions in logistics, healthcare, and customer service. It then examines the application of predictive maintenance in industrial settings, where AI-driven models prevent equipment failure, reduce costs, and improve safety. In human resources, AI powers workforce planning through predictive attrition models, resume analysis, and sentiment detection, shifting HR from an administrative role to a strategic partner.

As device populations expand, traditional perimeter-centric and zone-based security models fail, since trust can no longer be inferred from location and boundaries become increasingly diffuse. Threat actors exploit these limitations, using compromised devices to bypass defenses and enable lateral movement while concealing malicious behavior. Zero-trust principles provide an alternative by eliminating implicit trust and requiring continuous verification for every entity. This chapter per the authors outlines how Zero Trust concepts can be adapted to AIoT architectures across device, edge and cloud layers. It proposes model frameworks incorporating AI-based trust scoring, policy evaluation mechanisms, behavioral micro-segmentation, and device-aware trust controls, while examining related concerns including performance impact, real-time trust agility, and system overhead.

It further explores mitigation strategies including security-by-design, zero-trust networking, robust AI pipelines, supply-chain assurance, and emerging advancements such as digital twins, federated learning, explainable AI, and post-quantum cryptography. العنوان (title): PatternMiner: A Hybrid Deep Learning Framework for Fragment Classification and Pattern Recognition in Digital Forensics
المؤلفون (authors): Yousef K. Sanjalawe; Budoor Ahmad Allehyani; Sharif Naser Makhadmeh; Salam Al-E’mari; Ola Surakhi; Dima Suleiman
الانتماءات (affiliations): University of Jordan; Umm al-Qura University; Petra University; American University of Madaba
الكلمات المفتاحية (author_keywords): digital forensics; pattern recognition; block fragmentation; deep learning; transformer
الملخص (abstract): The growing fragmentation of digital evidence in modern computing environments poses significant challenges for digital forensic analysis. Data is often deleted, overwritten, or distributed across heterogeneous platforms, limiting the effectiveness of traditional forensic tools that rely on intact files and deterministic rules. This work addresses a key limitation in current forensic methodologies: the scarcity of learning-based approaches capable of identifying patterns in fragmented and incomplete digital evidence. To address this challenge, we propose PatternMiner, a hybrid deep learning framework that integrates Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs), Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks, and Transformer encoders. The framework combines byte-level content fragments with contextual metadata, such as timestamps and file permissions, enabling multimodal inference from fragmented data while explicitly excluding label-derived features to prevent leakage. PatternMiner is evaluated on established forensic benchmark datasets, including Digital Corpora and AFF4 forensic containers, which simulate realistic fragmentation scenarios. All experiments are conducted under an explicit leakage-controlled evaluation protocol with group-aware data partitioning to ensure that performance reflects generalization to unseen data. Results show that the proposed framework achieves strong performance, with an accuracy of 92.1% and a macro-averaged F1-score of 92.1% under complete input conditions. Furthermore, the model demonstrates resilience to degraded and partially corrupted inputs, including truncation, byte removal, shifting, and fragment reordering. These findings indicate that PatternMiner effectively captures structural and contextual patterns in fragmented data, providing a practical step toward more reliable and data-driven forensic analysis. By combining multimodal learning with rigorous evaluation practices, the proposed framework contributes to developing scalable and generalizable solutions for modern digital forensic environments.

Task scheduling and resource allocation are core to this problem, and they are intricately coupled, especially when dealing with workflow-based applications that involve complex task dependencies. On the other hand, as cloud data sensitivity increases, there is a need to implement security solutions with non-negligible computational costs, making this problem even more challenging. The current state of the art involves determining task scheduling, resource allocation, and security enforcement as separate optimization processes, making this problem difficult to adapt and globally efficient. The paper introduces a "Security-Aware Graph-Based Learning Framework" to jointly address task scheduling and resource allocation in cloud computing environments. The proposed solution uses a graph-based system model that incorporates task dependencies and resource interactions as an explicit graph structure. The proposed solution uses a centralized decision policy learned through a simultaneous optimization of task mapping, resource allocation, and security-level decisions, with overall efficiency, energy, SLS agreement, and security as core goals. The proposed approach incorporates security awareness into its optimization process, accounting for task sensitivity and virtual machine trust levels.

الكلمات المفتاحية (author_keywords): artificial immune systems; anomaly detection; IoT network security; intrusion detection; zero-day attacks; negative selection; immunological memory; unsupervised learning; IoT-23 dataset; resource-constrained environments
الملخص (abstract): The rapid proliferation of Internet of Things (IoT) devices has significantly increased the attack surface of modern networks, making efficient and adaptive intrusion detection a critical requirement. Most existing IoT intrusion detection systems rely on supervised machine learning or deep learning models that require large volumes of labeled attack data and high computational resources, which limits their ability to detect zero-day attacks and operate in resource-constrained environments. In this article, an Artificial Immune System (AIS)-based anomaly detection scheme for protecting the security of IoT networks is introduced, using the practical dataset IoT-23. The novel scheme will define normal behavior of the IoT network using normal traffic data by employing Negative Selection, Immune Clone Selection, and the capabilities of immune memory to reflect anomalous behavior as an attack on the network’s self-profile. Flow-level statistical attributes will be extracted from Zeek log files after preprocessing, with variance-based features applied to improve efficiency. Performance evaluation on the IoT-23 dataset indicates that the novel scheme, which leverages AIS capabilities, achieves a competitive accuracy of 97.9% and an F1 Score of 97% without supervision. Additionally, the scheme places less emphasis on computationally intensive computations, offering greater adaptability to novel attacks without the use of supervision or deep learning techniques, making it most effective for real-world use.

العنوان (title): Forensic-BERT: Explainable Transformer-Based Detection of Concealed Evidence in Cross-Platform Volatile Memory
المؤلفون (authors): Yousef K. Sanjalawe; Salam Al-E’mari; Sharif Naser Makhadmeh
الانتماءات (affiliations): University of Jordan; Petra University
الكلمات المفتاحية (author_keywords): AI-driven forensic framework; disk forensics; entropy-based filtering; explainable AI; Forensic-BERT; memory analysis
الملخص (abstract): Advanced cyber threats increasingly exploit volatile memory to execute malicious payloads without touching persistent storage, rendering traditional disk-centric forensic tools insufficient for comprehensive digital investigations. This paper presents Forensic-BERT, an AI-driven forensic framework that automatically extracts and classifies potentially relevant artifacts from unstructured memory dumps across heterogeneous operating environments. The framework combines byte-boundary-preserving Hex-to-ASCII conversion, sliding-window Shannon entropy filtering (H > 7.2 bits per byte, 256-byte windows) to isolate high-probability artifact regions, and a binary-aware WordPiece tokenizer extended with 2048 domain-specific tokens covering hexadecimal byte patterns, Windows API names, and Linux system-call sequences. These components feed a transformer-based classifier fine-tuned from bert-base-uncased (110 M parameters) on memory-derived text, with sliding-window inference and majority-vote aggregation for large images. A SHAP DeepExplainer module and averaged 12-head attention heatmaps provide transparent, analyst-accessible explanations for classification decisions. We evaluate the framework on a multi-source corpus of 735 labeled memory segments drawn from 197 distinct images across four independent collections, MemLabs, the DARPA Transparent Computing program, Digital Corpora, and live sandbox execution traces from Any.run and Joe Sandbox, spanning Windows XP through Windows 11, Ubuntu Linux 16.04/18.04, and FreeBSD. Source-stratified five-fold cross-validation yields an overall F1-score of 0.92 +/- 0.02 and AUC-ROC of 0.95 +/- 0.01 (95% CI). Forensic-BERT outperforms all six baselines, Volatility with YARA rules (F1 = 0.71), Random Forest (F1 = 0.82), BiLSTM with GloVe embeddings (F1 = 0.85), MRm-DLDet (F1 = 0.87), SPECTRE (F1 = 0.89), and SecBERT (F1 = 0.90), with every pairwise difference statistically significant under the McNemar test with Bonferroni correction. Explainability quality is independently confirmed by a Spearman rank correlation of rho = 0.81 between model SHAP token rankings and expert forensic-indicator rankings and by a System Usability Scale score of 73.2 among certified examiners. The complete pipeline processes 512 MB memory images in 7.5-10.2 s (GPU) or 38-52 s (CPU-only), scaling to 4 GB images with near-linear throughput. These results indicate that, on the corpus evaluated here, combining domain-adapted NLP preprocessing, transformer-based sequence modeling, and quantified explainability can improve the effectiveness and usability of analyst decision support and investigative triage for volatile memory analysis.

العنوان (title): Secure intrusion detection system for industrial control systems using digital twins
المؤلفون (authors): Yousef K. Sanjalawe; Sharif Naser Makhadmeh; Salam Al-E’mari; Emran Abdulsalam Alzubi

الملخص (abstract): Industrial Control Systems (ICS) are increasingly exposed to sophisticated cyber-physical attacks that traditional Intrusion Detection Systems (IDS) often fail to detect due to their limited awareness of physical process dynamics. To address this challenge, we propose a Digital Twin (DT)-enabled IDS framework that combines deep learning with real-time process simulation. Specifically, the detection algorithm is implemented using a hybrid model that integrates a Temporal Convolutional Network (TCN) to extract short-term temporal dependencies and a Transformer encoder to capture long-range semantic relationships. A feature-level fusion strategy unifies cyber data (network/application logs) and physical process data (sensor/actuator signals) into a shared representation, which is then classified by the TCN-Transformer model. The system is further optimized using the Tornado Optimizer, a bio-inspired metaheuristic that automatically tunes hyperparameters to improve accuracy and generalization. Experiments conducted on two benchmark datasets, Honeypot 2022 (cyber-only) and SWaT (cyber-physical), demonstrate that the proposed framework achieves 97.2% accuracy and a 96.9% F1-score on the SWaT dataset. The model consistently outperforms the evaluated representative baseline IDS methods under identical experimental conditions. Robustness analysis further confirms its resilience to noise, missing data, and adversarial perturbations.

Traditional tokenization techniques used for password analysis frequently overlook or misclassify symbolic and numeric elements, resulting in incomplete strength evaluations and less effective cracking strategies. This study presents a Breadth-First Search (BFS)-based tokenization framework that systematically segments passwords into meaningful components, including words from dictionaries, numeric sequences, and symbolic tokens. The BFS algorithm examines all possible substring combinations to identify the most comprehensive segmentation path. Remaining unmatched symbols and numbers are processed in a dedicated post-analysis phase to ensure complete token representation. Experiments conducted on a real-world dataset of 100,000 passwords demonstrate that the proposed approach outperforms baseline tokenizers in terms of token coverage and segmentation accuracy, while maintaining efficient processing times. The improved tokenization results contribute to a more accurate assessment of password complexity and support the development of stronger password-cracking models. These findings emphasize the importance of structure-aware parsing methods in advancing password security analysis.

This chapter argues that failures in maintaining user security during AI-driven digital transformation primarily stem from socio-technical challenges involving automated systems, organizational processes, and human decision-making. العنوان (title): Physics-Informed Neural Networks in Computational Mechanics: A Critical Review of Stability, Generalization, and Multi-Scale Applications
المجلة أو المؤتمر (venue): Archives of Computational Methods in Engineering
المؤلفون (authors): Yousef K. Sanjalawe; Salam Al-E’mari; Sharif Naser Makhadmeh
الانتماءات (affiliations): University of Jordan; Petra University
الكلمات المفتاحية (author_keywords): physics-informed neural networks; neural tangent kernel; spectral bias; causality violation; discontinuity handling; inverse problems; multi-physics coupling; fluid-structure interaction; fracture mechanics; uncertainty quantification; multiscale modeling; generalization
كلمات الفهرسة (keywords_plus): DEEP LEARNING FRAMEWORK
الملخص (abstract): Solving partial differential equations numerically has long been the province of mesh-based methods, yet the last several years have seen Physics-Informed Neural Networks (pinns) emerge as a genuinely different kind of alternative, one that encodes the governing equations directly into the loss function of a neural network and, in doing so, sidesteps the mesh-generation bottleneck that consumes so much engineering time in classical workflows. The appeal is real, but so are the limitations, and the gap between what pinns promise and what they reliably deliver in practice remains, in our view, wider than much of the current literature acknowledges. This review attempts to close that gap, or at least to map it honestly. We cast the pinn training problem in the language of numerical analysis, formalizing the composite residual functional, tracing training dynamics through the neural tangent kernel, and deriving Sobolev-norm stability bounds that connect what the optimizer minimizes to what the engineer actually needs. Along the way, we identify five recurring failure modes: spectral bias, gradient pathology, landscape stiffness, causality violation, and breakdown near discontinuities, and for each, we provide both a quantitative diagnostic and a remediation validated in the literature. Head-to-head benchmarks against finite element, finite volume, and boundary element solvers show that high-order classical methods routinely outperform pinns on smooth problems by several orders of magnitude; yet pinns hold clear advantages in inverse identification, high-dimensional settings, and geometrically evolving domains. We survey the state of the art in fracture mechanics, multi-physics coupling, fluid-structure interaction, and uncertainty quantification, and argue that hybrid fem-pinn architectures currently offer the most credible path toward industrial use. Unresolved theoretical and computational barriers are identified throughout.

الكلمات المفتاحية (author_keywords): cognitive computing; neuro-symbolic AI; decision intelligence; human cognition; statistical learning; cognitive reasoning; brain-inspired architecture; interpretability; trust in AI; uncertainty
الملخص (abstract): Artificial intelligence systems are increasingly used for complex decision-making in domains characterized by uncertainty, scale, and dynamic change. While traditional algorithm-based approaches have achieved strong performance in data-driven tasks, they remain limited in flexibility, contextual awareness, and interpretability when compared with human cognition. At the same time, advances in neuroscience and cognitive science have clarified the mechanisms of perception, learning, memory, attention, and reasoning that underlie human decision-making. This chapter examines how such cognitive principles can be translated into computational models that bridge statistical learning and cognitive reasoning. Drawing on cognitive computing and neuro-symbolic AI, it proposes an integrative framework for AI-supported decision intelligence that combines data-driven learning with brain-inspired architectures, emphasizing transparency, trust, and cognitive responsibility in the design of interpretable and context-sensitive intelligent systems.

العنوان (title): Goal-Oriented Semantic Communication Over Fluid Antenna Systems: Framework, Optimization, and Performance Bounds Under Imperfect CSI

المؤلفون (authors): Yousef K. Sanjalawe; Sharif Naser Makhadmeh; Salam Al-E’mari; Muder Almiani
الانتماءات (affiliations): University of Jordan; Petra University; Gulf University for Science & Technology
الكلمات المفتاحية (author_keywords): Ports (computers); Modeling; Optimization; Signal to noise ratio; Antennas; Energy; Joints; Weighted sum model; Fluids; Floors; Fluid antenna system; goal-oriented communication; semantic communication; imperfect CSI; Fisher-Snedecor fading
الملخص (abstract): This paper proposes GoSemFAS, the first unified framework for goal-oriented semantic communication over Fluid Antenna Systems (FAS) with imperfect Channel State Information (CSI). A single-RF-chain transmitter with N-p software-reconfigurable ports jointly optimizes port selection, semantic compression ratio rho , and transmit power P to maximize a semantic effectiveness metric that balances task inference accuracy against energy consumption. Channel estimation errors are captured via a bounded-uncertainty model with radius epsilon , and the propagation channel is characterized by the Fisher-Snedecor F composite fading distribution, which jointly encompasses Nakagami- m small-scale fading and inverse-Nakagami shadowing. Tight closed-form expressions for the Semantic Outage Probability (SOP) and the average Goal-Completion Rate (GCR) are derived using Meijer-G representations, establishing an effective diversity order of min{N-p, [2L] + 1} & centerdot; m, full N-p-fold port diversity for sufficiently spaced ports, saturating at the aperture degrees-of-freedom limit under dense packing, together with an exact characterization of the CSI-induced outage floor and a pilot-power scaling law that provably preserves full diversity. The spatial dependence among ports is further characterized exactly through a copula-based analysis: a Gaussian copula formulation yields the exact SOP under arbitrary port correlations, while a Farlie-Gumbel-Morgenstern (FGM) copula provides a closed-form alternative that certifies the tightness of the inclusion-exclusion approximation. An Alternating Optimization (AO) algorithm decomposes the non-convex joint problem into three globally solvable sub-problems: closed-form port selection, closed-form power-law power control, and closed-form compression ratio update, with provable monotone convergence and O(N-p) per-iteration complexity. A three-way Pareto analysis characterizes the fundamental distortion-rate-energy trade-off across three operating regimes. Numerical results validate all analytical and asymptotic expressions against Monte Carlo simulation and demonstrate that GoSemFAS achieves 31% lower energy per correct inference, 68% higher semantic energy efficiency, and a 44% wider CSI robustness margin compared with fixed-antenna baselines, while attaining 97% of the goal-completion rate of a full N-p -branch maximum-ratio-combining (MRC) array, and a strictly higher hardware-aware semantic energy efficiency, using a single RF chain.

العنوان (title): MEPO-SLM: multi-objective evolutionary prompt optimization for energy-efficient small language models on edge devices
المؤلفون (authors): Yousef K. Sanjalawe; Salam Al-E’mari; Sharif Naser Makhadmeh
الانتماءات (affiliations): University of Jordan; Petra University
الكلمات المفتاحية (author_keywords): Evolutionary computation; Multi-objective optimization; Prompt engineering; Small language models; Edge AI; Energy efficiency; Hallucination reduction; NSGA-II; NLP; Pareto optimization; Arabic NLP
كلمات الفهرسة (keywords_plus): ALGORITHM; SELECTION
الملخص (abstract): Deploying small language models (SLMs) on edge hardware requires simultaneously meeting four conflicting requirements: high task accuracy, low hallucination rate, bounded inference latency, and minimal energy consumption. We present MEPO-SLM, a framework that reformulates prompt engineering for SLMs as a four-objective Pareto problem over task inaccuracy (), hallucination rate (), per-query latency (), and per-query energy (). Prompts are represented as five-segment genomes, varied by four coordinated operators, including a directed length operator and a Hallucination-Aware Perturbation repair operator, and kept diverse in objective and prompt-embedding space. We evaluate Phi-3-mini and Gemma-2B on English TriviaQA and Arabic medical QA, and TinyLlama-1.1B on TriviaQA only, using Raspberry Pi 5 and NVIDIA Jetson Orin Nano measurements. Across the reported settings, MEPO-SLM improves accuracy by up to 12.3 percentage points, reduces hallucination by up to 41.2% relative, and reduces per-query energy by up to 28.4%. On the reference Phi-3-mini/TriviaQA setting, hypervolume is 57.3% higher than MOPrompt, the strongest bi-objective baseline, and 43.7% higher than GEPA, the strongest non-MEPO-SLM comparator. Statistical tests are restricted to explicitly repeated, paired experiments; single-run hardware results are reported descriptively. To our knowledge, no prior APO framework jointly optimizes all four objectives on edge hardware for both English and Arabic NLP.

العنوان (title): Quantum-Inspired Deep Learning for Automated Software Defect Prediction: A Hybrid QLSTM-GCN Approach
المجلة أو المؤتمر (venue): International Journal of Computational Intelligence Systems
المؤلفون (authors): Yousef K. Sanjalawe; Salam Al-E’mari; Salam Fraihat; Qusai Yousef Shambour; Sharif Naser Makhadmeh
الانتماءات (affiliations): University of Jordan; Petra University; Ajman University; Middle East University
الكلمات المفتاحية (author_keywords): software defect prediction; graph convolutional networks; hybrid neural network; quantum genetic algorithm; feature selection; explainable AI; SHAP; lime; partial dependence plots; class imbalance
الملخص (abstract): The growing complexity of contemporary software systems has intensified the need for intelligent and dependable techniques capable of identifying defects early. Conventional machine learning models often face limitations when handling high-dimensional code metrics, class imbalance, and limited interpretability, thereby diminishing their practical utility. More critically, existing approaches treat software defect prediction as a flat-feature classification problem, failing to jointly model the temporal evolution of software metrics and the structural dependencies between modules, two complementary dimensions that empirical evidence consistently identifies as the primary drivers of defect propagation in real-world repositories. In this study, we propose a quantum-inspired hybrid deep learning framework, QLSTM-GCN, that combines the sequential modeling strength of Quantum Long Short-Term Memory (QLSTM) networks with the structural learning capacity of Graph Convolutional Networks (GCNs). Importantly, all quantum-inspired operations are numerically simulated on classical hardware using unitary matrix transformations, requiring no quantum computing infrastructure and ensuring full reproducibility on standard computing platforms. This integration enables the simultaneous capture of temporal and topological dependencies inherent in software repositories. To refine the input space, an improved Quantum-Inspired Genetic Algorithm (QIGA) is applied for optimized feature selection, reducing feature dimensionality by 37-39% while improving both accuracy and model generalization across datasets. Furthermore, explainable AI mechanisms, including Local Interpretable Model-Agnostic Explanations (LIME), Partial Dependence Plots (PDP), and SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP), are incorporated to enhance interpretability and transparency at both the instance and global levels. Experiments conducted on three benchmark datasets, NASA PROMISE, GitHub Bug, and GHPR, demonstrate that QLSTM-GCN attains a peak accuracy of 96.7% and an AUC-ROC of 98.7% on the NASA PROMISE dataset, with consistently strong performance across all three benchmarks (95.3%-96.7% accuracy; 98.1%-98.7% AUC-ROC), surpassing recent state-of-the-art approaches on every evaluated metric. More importantly, the framework improves reliability and trust in software quality assurance by balancing predictive performance with practical explainability, offering actionable insights at the module, project, and organizational levels.

العنوان (title): Explainable Graph Neural Networks for Multi-Class Fraudulent Address Classification in Ethereum
المؤلفون (authors): Salam Al-E’mari; Yousef K. Sanjalawe; Salam Fraihat; Ahd Aljarf
الانتماءات (affiliations): Petra University; University of Jordan; Ajman University; Umm al-Qura University
الكلمات المفتاحية (author_keywords): Ethereum fraud detection; graph neural networks; GraphSAGE; BLTE dataset; GNNExplainer; explainable artificial intelligence
الملخص (abstract): Blockchain networks have become a major target for fraudulent activities, including phishing and scamming attacks, due to the irreversible and pseudonymous nature of cryptocurrency transactions. Existing Ethereum fraud detection studies commonly formulate the problem as a binary classification task, which limits their ability to distinguish among different malicious behaviors. This paper proposes an explainable Graph Neural Network-based framework for multi-class Ethereum address classification using an enhanced version of the Benchmark Labeled Transactions Ethereum (BLTE) dataset. The original binary BLTE dataset is extended into a multi-class dataset by integrating external attack-category information and labeling addresses as Normal, Phishing, or Scamming. The resulting BLTE multi-class dataset contains 73,033 Ethereum addresses, 23 behavioral node features, and 6588 directed transaction edges. Three GNN architectures, namely Graph Attention Network (GAT), Graph Convolutional Network (GCN), and GraphSAGE, are evaluated under identical experimental settings. Across ten stratified random seeds, GraphSAGE achieves the best overall performance among the implemented GNNs, with 98.84 +/- 0.06% accuracy, 80.42 +/- 2.67% macro recall, 51.08 +/- 1.54% macro F1-score, and 99.27 +/- 0.03% weighted F1-score. To improve model transparency, GNNExplainer is used to identify influential transaction subgraphs and important node features that contribute to each prediction. The results indicate that neighborhood-aware graph learning is useful for multi-class Ethereum address classification, while also showing that minority-class precision remains challenging under severe class imbalance. A feature-only multilayer perceptron is found to be a strong baseline whose macro F1-score is statistically indistinguishable from GraphSAGE after multiple-comparison correction; the improvement attributable to graph structure is therefore modest and concentrated on the small connected portion of the network, and external validation on independent datasets is still required before the framework is used in real investigations.

العنوان (title): A Digital Twin and Lightweight Blockchain Logging Framework for Real-Time CPS Threat Detection
المؤلفون (authors): Salam Al-E’mari; Yousef K. Sanjalawe; Budoor Ahmad Allehyani; Ahd Aljarf; Fares Alharbi
الانتماءات (affiliations): University of Jordan; Umm al-Qura University; Shaqra University
الكلمات المفتاحية (author_keywords): cyber-physical security; digital twin; anomaly detection; threat detection; hash chains; lightweight inference; rule-based verification; Industrial Internet of Things; resource-constrained environments; real-time security monitoring
الملخص (abstract): Cyber-Physical Systems (CPS), including Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) environments and smart infrastructures, are increasingly vulnerable to sophisticated cyberattacks due to their heterogeneous architectures, large-scale deployments, and strict real-time operational constraints.Conventional security mechanisms often struggle to provide low-latency threat detection, continuous monitoring, and reliable forensic traceability under resourceconstrained conditions.This paper presents a lightweight Digital Twin (DT)-driven cybersecurity framework that integrates synchronized DT state modeling, hybrid anomaly detection, and tamper-evident audit logging for real-time CPS threat detection.Within this framework, the DT is realized as an operational, data-driven twin whose role is continuous bidirectional state synchronization, integrity-aware feature abstraction, and context-aware representation of CPS assets for detection, rather than a physics-based simulation, "what-if " scenario, or predictive-maintenance twin; these richer capabilities are enabled by the modular DT design and are identified as future extensions.The proposed framework employs a decoupled training-deployment strategy in which Isolation Forest (IF), Gradient Boosting Machine (GBM), and Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP) models are combined during an offline ensemble calibration stage to optimize detection thresholds, while only a lightweight MLP model is executed during runtime inference to minimize computational overhead.To enhance detection reliability and interpretability, the learning-based detection pipeline is further augmented with domain-aware rule-based verification.In addition, validated security events are recorded via a lightweight, hash-chained, append-only logging mechanism that provides tamper-evident forensic traceability without the latency overhead of consensus-driven distributed ledger systems.Experimental evaluation on controlled synthetic CPS telemetry achieved 99.6% detection accuracy, 99.5% precision, 99.8% recall, and an F1-score of 99.6%.The framework was further validated on three real-world industrial CPS benchmarks (SWaT, WADI, and BATADAL), where F1-scores ranged from 0.976 to 0.986, demonstrating consistent generalization across heterogeneous operational environments.In addition, the proposed architecture sustained telemetry processing rates exceeding 5000 events per minute with an average logging latency of 0.84 s and CPU utilization below 65%.These results demonstrate that the proposed framework provides an efficient and practically deployable CPS security architecture that balances lightweight runtime inference, detection reliability, and forensic auditability in resource-constrained environments.

العنوان (title): ENTRUST: Closed-Loop Trust-Calibrated Autonomous Cyber Defense for Ambient IoT
المؤلفون (authors): Yousef K. Sanjalawe; Salam Al-E’mari; Muder Almiani
الانتماءات (affiliations): University of Jordan; Petra University; Gulf University for Science & Technology
الكلمات المفتاحية (author_keywords): ambient IoT; autonomous cyber defense; human-AI teaming; trust calibration; explainable AI; adaptive autonomy; intrusion detection; uncertainty quantification; human-in-the-loop; trustworthy AI
الملخص (abstract): Ambient Internet-of-Things (IoT) deployments place large fleets of battery-less, energy-harvesting devices in environments where human operators cannot review every security event. Autonomous Artificial-Intelligence (AI) defenders can reduce this burden, but incorrect autonomous containment can amplify incidents, whereas excessive deferral can overwhelm operators and distort appropriate reliance. Existing approaches typically configure detection, explanation, and autonomy separately. We present ENTRUST, which treats these capabilities as a closed-loop control problem. A calibrated detector estimates threat probability together with epistemic and aleatoric uncertainty. A trust-calibration controller tracks the gap between operator trust and the agent's estimated reliability. A constrained co-adaptation policy then jointly selects one of five autonomy levels and one of four explanation-fidelity levels, subject to hard safety invariants for critical and irreversible actions. We formalize the problem and provide the co-adaptation and trust-update algorithms. The evaluation is simulation-based and uses an episodic simulator whose attack taxonomy, class priors, and device-criticality structure follow public IoT intrusion corpora. The reported numerical results should therefore be interpreted as comparative estimates under controlled conditions, not as measurements from a deployed ambient-IoT system. Across five threat conditions, 30 seeds, five baselines, and nine ablations, ENTRUST attains the lowest harmful-action rate and trust-calibration error in every evaluated condition while requiring roughly 70% fewer human interventions than mandatory-approval oversight. Under adversarial context injection, containment remains at 0.74 , compared with 0.64 for unconstrained autonomy (Cliff's delta=1.0 , p<10(-10 )). The nine ablations further isolate the mechanism: adaptive autonomy primarily affects safety, detection-explanation-autonomy coupling affects calibration, and uncertainty plus trust feedback affect adversarial robustness.

المجلة أو المؤتمر (venue): Advances in computational intelligence and robotics book series

الملخص (abstract): Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly shaping assessment practices in higher education through tools such as automated grading systems, AI-generated feedback, learning analytics, and technologies designed to detect academic dishonesty. While these innovations promise greater efficiency, scalability, and consistency in evaluating student performance, they also introduce significant challenges related to fairness, transparency, academic integrity, and institutional governance. This chapter argues that the central challenge of AI-mediated assessment is not purely technological but lies in the governance of trust within assessment systems. Furthermore, it examines how AI reshapes power relations among educators, students, institutions, and technological systems, while highlighting issues such as algorithmic bias, surveillance-oriented integrity technologies, and unequal global adoption of AI.

العنوان (title): When Does Representation Learning Help Attack-Path Forecasting? A Controlled Multi-Cloud Study with CAPTURE-MC
المؤلفون (authors): Salam Al-E’mari; Yousef K. Sanjalawe; Muder Almiani; Mohammad Abdallah Alsharaiah
الانتماءات (affiliations): Petra University; University of Jordan; Gulf University for Science & Technology
الكلمات المفتاحية (author_keywords): multi-cloud security; MITRE ATT&CK; first-order Markov model; conformal prediction; adversarial robustness
الملخص (abstract): Cloud defenders increasingly want to anticipate an attacker’s next move, not merely detect the last one. We study attack-path forecasting in multi-cloud environments: given the partial trace of an in-progress campaign, predict the next ATT&CK technique. We present CAPTURE-MC, a heterogeneous temporal-graph model that encodes cross-provider telemetry and forecasts the next technique under a transition prior, and we release MC-PathBench, a synthetic but structurally faithful benchmark with four leakage-controlled generalization splits (temporal, cross-cloud, unseen-composition, and campaign hold-out). Our central contribution is an honest, carefully controlled account of when learned temporal-graph representations help and when they do not. We find that the technique-transition structure is a very strong predictor: when the attacker’s current technique is known, a first-order Markov model and a uniform-over-allowed-transitions rule match or exceed CAPTURE-MC and a temporal-graph network, so the deep models add little in that idealized regime. The picture reverses in the realistic regime where the current technique must be inferred: as current-technique certainty degrades, the structural baselines, indexed entirely by it, collapse toward chance, whereas CAPTURE-MC degrades gracefully and nearly doubles their accuracy when the current technique is unknown. CAPTURE-MC is likewise robust to a substantially corrupted transition prior (missing, spurious, or misdirected edges). We also report, transparently, where CAPTURE-MC does not help: gradient-boosted trees remain the best per-event and campaign-level detectors; next-entity and time-to-transition prediction are at chance for every model; and the conformal layer, while achieving coverage, yields prediction sets larger than the list of allowed successors and so is not an efficiency gain. The prior is estimated only from training data, never the generator’s graph, which removes a leakage path present in an earlier version of this work and changes several conclusions. The practical lesson for predictive cloud defense is that structural baselines are strong and must be reported, and that the value of representation learning appears precisely where structural assumptions break down.

العنوان (title): MobiTrust: Risk-Bounded Adaptive Split Inference Under Mobility, Privacy Leakage, and Latent-Space Attacks
المؤلفون (authors): Salam Al-E’mari; Yousef K. Sanjalawe; Muder Almiani; Mohammad Abdallah Alsharaiah
الانتماءات (affiliations): Petra University; University of Jordan; Gulf University for Science & Technology
الكلمات المفتاحية (author_keywords): split inference; privacy leakage; edge servers; membership inference attacks; attribute inference attacks; mobile devices; adversarial robustness
الملخص (abstract): Split inference lets a mobile device run the first layers of a neural network locally and hand the intermediate representation to an edge server, trading raw data disclosure for communication and offloaded computation. The common assumption that keeping raw inputs on the device is enough for privacy does not survive contact with modern attacks: intermediate activations can be inverted back to inputs, tested for membership, or probed for sensitive attributes, and they can be tampered with in transit. These risks are not fixed properties of a network; they shift with the split point, with any protection applied to the representation, with the trust placed in the serving edge, and with the sensitive attributes at stake in a given context. Schedulers that pick a split to minimise latency or energy, or that fold risk into a single weighted objective, routinely cross privacy and integrity limits whenever the network briefly makes offloading attractive. We present MobiTrust, an adaptive split-inference controller that treats privacy and latent-integrity risk as explicit constraints on measured risk scores rather than terms to be traded away. Two measurable quantities drive it: Context-Dependent Semantic Exposure (CDSE), a worst-channel estimate of privacy leakage (assembled from reconstruction, shadow-model membership, and attribute attacks) that accounts for the sensitive attributes a deployment cares about, and Latent Integrity Risk (LIR), a detector score for tampered representations. A feasibility-filtering controller selects, at each inference, the split point, the representation protection, and the serving edge that minimise cost subject to per-inference risk and deadline budgets, and it falls back to on-device execution when no offload is safe. We frame this as a controlled simulation study of the constraint mechanism: it runs on a reduced-scale, fully reproducible testbed with an image and a sensing workload and a transparent analytical latency/energy model, so the claims concern the controller’s decisions and their effect on measured risk, not absolute timings on a particular device. CDSE tracks measured attack success far better than the split-depth and tensor-size heuristics used by leakage-agnostic schedulers (Spearman ρ of 0.59 and 0.87 versus 0.33 and 0.72 for depth). Over mixed mobility traces, MobiTrust holds the profiled privacy and adversarial constraint violations at 0% while the latency-only and weighted-sum baselines violate the privacy budget in 88% of inferences and the integrity budget in up to 58%; a weight sweep shows that, across the weightings we tested, the weighted-sum baseline reaches zero violations only by ceasing to offload. The cost of the guarantee is energy: MobiTrust saves device energy by offloading when it is safe, but a zero-violation local-only baseline attains higher accuracy and lower tail latency, so the improvement is a favourable energy trade-off rather than a uniform win. Because zero violations certify compliance with the profiled risk scores rather than an independently validated security bound, we also show that, under estimation uncertainty, the controller’s primal–dual margin holds the realised violation rate at its tolerance.

العنوان (title): XAI for Financial Sustainability Assessment and Prediction in Higher Education Institutions
المؤلفون (authors): Budoor Ahmad Allehyani; Salam Al-E’mari
الانتماءات (affiliations): Umm al-Qura University; Petra University
الكلمات المفتاحية (author_keywords): financial sustainability; higher education institutions; explainable AI; key performance indicators; financial distress prediction; anomaly detection; income diversification; random forest; Isolation Forest; financial benchmarking
الملخص (abstract): Financial sustainability is a growing concern for Higher Education Institutions (HEIs). Many institutions face structural financial pressures due to reduced public funding, volatile enrolment, and rising costs. Although institutions collect increasing amounts of financial data, sustainability assessments often rely on backward-looking accounting ratios and provide limited insight into future patterns. Rather than proposing a new machine-learning algorithm, this study integrates and empirically evaluates established, complementary analytical techniques within one framework: financial Key Performance Indicator (KPI) engineering, a Financial Sustainability Index (FSI), machine-learning prediction, relative sustainability classification, institutional clustering, anomaly detection, and Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI). Using the public Higher Education Statistics Agency finance collection, we constructed a longitudinal dataset containing 2207 provider-year observations and examined income diversification, funding dependency, research activity, growth, and capital investment. Supervised prediction was evaluated on 1880 longitudinal records using leakage-safe expanding-window temporal validation. Across 1387 out-of-time observations, the persistence baseline achieved the strongest performance, with an R2 of 0.868, an MAE of 1.332, and an RMSE of 2.462. The Random Forest model remained strongly predictive, achieving an R2 of 0.852, an MAE of 1.587, and an RMSE of 2.612, while demonstrating stable performance across 30 random seeds. Temporal relative-sustainability classification achieved a mean accuracy of 0.842 and a macro-F1 score of 0.835. Unsupervised analysis identified three institutional profiles, while Isolation Forest flagged 111 financially atypical provider-year observations. Once current-year FSI was excluded, XAI analysis identified tuition dependency, income diversification, unrestricted reserves, and premises costs as the indicators on which predictions relied most. Because the FSI is internally constructed and the classification categories are sample-relative, the framework is presented as a proof-of-concept approach for sustainability screening and benchmarking rather than a validated predictor of financial distress.

الملخص (abstract): This systematic review examines methodological approaches to social media content analysis through analysis of 332 SCOPUS-indexed publications. We address three research questions: identifying predominant methodologies, tracing their temporal evolution, and evaluating AI’s role in current and future research. Through systematic coding of abstracts, we classified methodologies into five categories: Manual/Qualitative, Statistical/Rule-Based, Machine Learning, Deep Learning, and AI/Foundation Models. Results show Manual/Qualitative approaches remain most prevalent (32.5%), followed by Machine Learning (18.7%), Deep Learning (7.5%), AI/Foundation Models (6.3%), and Statistical/Rule-Based methods (5.4%). Temporal analysis reveals progressive integration of computational approaches, with recent years showing increased adoption of transformer-based models, including BERT and large language models. The analysis of future research directions identified 59 papers (17.8%) that explicitly mentioned future work, with 91.5% proposing AI-enhanced methodologies. AI-related terms dominated future work discussions, with 135 general AI mentions, 29 machine learning references, and 13 LLM mentions. These findings indicate strong momentum toward AI integration while traditional qualitative methods maintain importance, suggesting optimal approaches combine computational efficiency with human interpretive capabilities for comprehensive social media content analysis.

الملخص (abstract): This paper proposes a hybrid model that utilises supervised machine learning classification to facilitate Software Defect Prediction (SDP) process which aims to discover which parts of a software system may contain defects to provide in advance valuable information on software defects. The model was empirically tested through its application to NASA’s PROMISE software engineering repository datasets. By comparing the results of the proposed model with other relative approaches (Support Vector Machine (SVM), Random Forest (RF), Naïve Bayes (NB) algorithms as feature selectors and Decision Tree and Naïve Bayes (NB) as a classifier), the obtained results show an improved performance of the prediction process. الملخص (abstract): Viral hepatitis represents a major global health concern due to its progression during the early stages with the possibility to evolve into more severe liver diseases. This paper presents a comprehensive machine learning–based framework for early detection of viral hepatitis and its stage using clinical laboratory data. The findings confirm that machine learning algorithms can effectively support early viral hepatitis detection and disease stage classification, offering clinically meaningful decision support for healthcare systems.

الملخص (abstract): Model-based reinforcement learning combines neural networks with planning to achieve superhuman performance in board and video games. MuZero exemplifies this by learning a model and using Monte Carlo tree search (MCTS) for planning. However, its search component employs unstable prior normalization, stochastic action selection, and a fixed simulation budget, all of which limit performance and data efficiency, particularly in low-data regimes. We propose a hybrid optimization method called Hybrid MCTS++, which improves the search element of MuZero. The method computes numerically stable priors using a masked softmax over legal actions, deterministically selects actions by taking the maximum UCB score, and adapts the number of simulations according to the entropy of the root policy distribution. This adaptive schedule allocates more simulations when the search is uncertain and fewer when the model is confident. We mathematically formulate the algorithm, provide pseudocode, and evaluate it in the Tic-Tac-Toe environment included in the MuZero repository. Against a random opponent, our hybrid search achieved 100% accuracy and sensitivity, improving the baseline accuracy of MCTS of 74% accuracy and 69.8% sensitivity. Against an expert opponent, Hybrid MCTS++ reached 86% accuracy and 36.4% sensitivity compared to baseline’s 22% accuracy and 2.5% sensitivity. These results demonstrate that Hybrid MCTS++ markedly enhances search efficiency and predictive metrics without retraining underlying models, offering a simple yet powerful upgrade for model-based reinforcement learning systems overall.

الملخص (abstract): Detecting malicious activity in cloud networks is a critical defensive task for security operations centres (SOCs). In practice, intrusion detection systems must achieve strong detection performance while keeping false alarms low enough to remain operationally actionable, since high alert volumes can overwhelm analysts and delay response. This paper presents a fully reproducible machine–learning pipeline for intrusion detection using the NSL-KDD benchmark dataset, comparing baseline classifiers—logistic regression, random forests, support vector machines, gradient boosting, and multi-layer perceptrons—under repeated stratified cross-validation with consistent preprocessing and hyperparameter handling. Beyond fixed decision thresholds, we introduce a threshold-optimised (and optionally cost-sensitive) decision rule for logistic regression that selects an operating point to explicitly trade detection against false alarms. Experiments show that a random forest achieves the strongest overall performance (highest F1-score and MCC), while threshold optimisation meaningfully improves the precision–recall balance of logistic regression, illustrating a practical mechanism for adapting simpler models to SOC alerting constraints. الملخص (abstract): The increasing demand for electricity, driven by the proliferation of modern appliances, has placed significant strain on traditional power grids. Smart Grids have emerged as a viable solution to this challenge, particularly through intelligent demand-side energy management strategies such as the Appliance Energy Scheduling Problem (AESP). This study formulates AESP as a complex multi-objective optimization problem that seeks to minimize electricity bills, waiting time rate (WTR), capacity energy rate (CER), and the peak-to-average ratio, while maximizing user comfort. To effectively solve this problem, a novel hybrid optimization algorithm is proposed, the White Shark Optimizer with Crossover (WSC), which combines the exploration–exploitation capabilities of the White Shark Optimizer (WSO) with the diversity-enhancing benefits of a crossover evolutionary operator. A non-Pareto scalarization-based approach is employed to manage the multiple conflicting objectives simultaneously. The proposed approach is implemented within a residential Internet of Things framework, enabling intelligent and efficient management of home appliances by facilitating real-time monitoring, control, and optimization of energy usage. The performance of WSC is benchmarked against four other hybrid metaheuristics across seven consumption scenarios and 149 appliances. Experimental results demonstrate that WSC outperforms all baseline and hybrid counterparts in terms of convergence speed, solution quality, and overall fitness. It achieved the lowest average fitness function (FF) value of 0.2014, with a corresponding reduction of 18.6% in WTR and 15.9% in CER compared to the next-best hybrid method. Additionally, WSC maintained competitive electricity bills and peak-to-average ratio values. Overall, the proposed WSC provides a stable and efficient solution for optimizing multi-objective energy scheduling in Smart Grid environments.

العنوان (title): Multi-Objective Harris Hawks Optimization: Principles, Variants, Applications, and Future Directions
رابط (url): https://Multi-objective optimization problems (MOPs) are common in practical scenarios where decision-makers need to accomplish several competing goals. Single-objective optimization techniques do not guarantee applicability in these scenarios. As such, there has been a need for the development of metaheuristics capable of generating multiple trade-off solutions. Harris Hawks Optimization (HHO) has been shown to possess strong exploration and exploitation capabilities for the solution of optimization problems, owing to the collaborative hunting tactics of Harris’s hawks. Therefore, the Multi-objective Harris Hawks Optimization (MHHO) algorithm was suggested to generalize HHO to handle MOPs. By combining the mechanisms of Pareto dominance, diversity preservation, elitism, adaptiveness, and others, MHHO approaches the Pareto-optimal front and provides decision-makers with several high-quality nondominated solutions. This study comprehensively examines MHHO, elaborating on its theoretical background, algorithmic variants, and fields of application. MHHO has been implemented in different disciplines. Using the Scopus database to conduct a bibliometric study, the publication growth, research development, and the application of MHHO in various fields of study were analyzed. By classifying the extant contributions into original, modified, and hybrid versions, the study provides a detailed outline of the algorithm’s progression. Applications spanning engineering, cloud computing, scheduling, networking, bioinformatics, and energy systems are analyzed, illustrating the broad adaptability of MHHO. A constructive critique has been conducted to evaluate some limitations including premature convergence, scalability issues, and difficulty in addressing disconnected Pareto regions. This review shows the versatility and potential of MHHO in tackling different optimization problems. In addition, further research is needed on the development of more sophisticated hybrid methods, tailored improvements, and more refined techniques for the preservation of diversity.

Therefore, the Multi-objective Harris Hawks Optimization (MHHO) algorithm was suggested to generalize HHO to handle MOPs. By combining the mechanisms of Pareto dominance, diversity preservation, elitism, adaptiveness, and others, MHHO approaches the Pareto-optimal front and provides decision-makers with several high-quality nondominated solutions. This study comprehensively examines MHHO, elaborating on its theoretical background, algorithmic variants, and fields of application. MHHO has been implemented in different disciplines. Using the Scopus database to conduct a bibliometric study, the publication growth, research development, and the application of MHHO in various fields of study were analyzed. By classifying the extant contributions into original, modified, and hybrid versions, the study provides a detailed outline of the algorithm's progression. Applications spanning engineering, cloud computing, scheduling, networking, bioinformatics, and energy systems are analyzed, illustrating the broad adaptability of MHHO. A constructive critique has been conducted to evaluate some limitations including premature convergence, scalability issues, and difficulty in addressing disconnected Pareto regions. This review shows the versatility and potential of MHHO in tackling different optimization problems. In addition, further research is needed on the development of more sophisticated hybrid methods, tailored improvements, and more refined techniques for the preservation of diversity.

Despite extensive research on machine-learning-based fraud detection, results are often difficult to compare because sampling, preprocessing, and metric choices can materially alter conclusions on highly imbalanced transaction data. This paper provides credit-card fraud detection using supervised and ensemble methods for on the widely used ULB/Worldline transaction dataset. We evaluate Logistic Regression, Linear Support Vector Machines, Random Forests, Gradient Boosting, Multi-Layer Perceptrons, and Extremely Randomized Trees, alongside an Isolation Forest anomaly-detection baseline. الملخص (abstract): Network intrusion detection systems (IDSs) complement preventive controls by monitoring traffic and raising alerts when malicious activity is suspected. While signature-based IDSs remain effective for known threats, they struggle with novel or obfuscated attacks and typically require continuous manual rule engineering. Machine-learning-based IDSs can learn complex traffic patterns, but published results often suffer from limited transparency, inconsistent experimental protocols, and weak reproducibility—especially on legacy benchmarks. In this paper, we present a reproducible, defensive pipeline for multi-class intrusion detection using the NSL–KDD benchmark derived from KDD’99. We evaluate four classical supervised learners (logistic regression, random forest, gradient boosting, and a shallow multi-layer perceptron) and propose a weighted soft-voting ensemble where weights are proportional to validation macro-F1scores to emphasize minority classes. On the official NSL–KDD test split, the ensemble attains accuracy 0.774, macro-F10.588, and weighted-F10.738, offering competitive performance relative to individual models. We further include an Isolation Forest baseline for binary anomaly detection and provide interpretable analyses including confusion matrices, ROC/precision– recall curves, feature importance, and learning curves. Overall, our study provides a transparent baseline and a defensively oriented reference implementation for future IDS research.

الملخص (abstract): Joint bandwidth and transmit-power allocation is a key enabler for latency- and energy-aware wireless services, but secrecy and quality-of-service (QoS) constraints make the resulting optimization nonconvex and difficult to solve at scale. This paper builds a compact benchmark for secure QoS-constrained bandwidth–power allocation and compares ten budgeted meta-heuristic optimizers: genetic algorithm (GA), particle swarm optimization (PSO), differential evolution (DE), grey wolf optimizer (GWO), simulated annealing (SA), ant colony optimization for continuous domains (ACOR), artificial bee colony (ABC), whale optimization algorithm (WOA), firefly algorithm (FA), and a hybrid adaptive DE–PSO variant (A-TBHyDEPSO). All methods are evaluated under an identical function-evaluation budget on a fixed K=8-user instance. Across 10 independent runs, GWO achieves the best mean penalized objective (12.656) but exhibits a feasibility rate of 70%, whereas A-TBHyDEPSO and FA achieve 100% feasibility with near-optimal objective values. Nonparametric tests confirm statistically significant performance differences among optimizers. The benchmark highlights a practical tradeoff between objective quality and constraint satisfaction in secrecy-aware resource allocation.
